clean_body: I think you should hear it| | | | | Patriot , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. Thank you for listening, and I hope I can count on your help. | | — John James Republican Nominee for Governor | | Paid for by John James for MI | | 35744 Van Dyke Avenue, Sterling Heights, MI 48312 The use of John James' military images, uniforms, or personnel does not imply endorsement by the Department of War or any branch of the U.S. military. |

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139119920/646295907/1834051724?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.09.13_Early-Memories_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNTFhYmRkNi04N2FmLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=l5AALtKrZ0pOAtZZGPIjUpsi_5RK1jCjbH54frrYECc=) Folks, from a very young age, my house was buzzing with conversation.

As I got older, I was part of those conversations about everything from gardening (my mother was an avid gardener) to ice skating (we lived next to a pond) to politics — local, state and national (my Dad taught government classes, and my mom eventually taught history in our local high school).

My parents volunteered on campaigns. All of which seemed totally normal to me — it’s what you did to do your part in a democracy. And that experience seeped into our home. My Dad would ask me from time to time: **_What are you doing for freedom today?_**

As a child, I didn’t know how to answer, so in between gulps of orange juice and whatever I was eating for breakfast that day I began pondering this big question.

As I helped my mom stuff envelopes with the local League of Women Voters, I don’t think I understood that such a mundane task was a critical form of citizenship. But I knew my dad’s question meant that we all had a responsibility to help shape the country we want to live in.

_At a time when costs are through the roof and our health care is under constant threat and this administration is running rampant with corruption and lawlessness, I hope we are all asking ourselves that central question:**What am I doing for freedom today?**_

[**_One way to fight for freedom is by fueling Democrats’ efforts to take back the majority by supporting the key battleground races that will decide Senate control. Every generation has a defining moment, one they carry with them for the rest of their lives. The one where time stops, the world changes, and all teens and adults remember where they were the moment they heard the news. These events tend to split time in a way that we thereafter demarcate life as before or after it. For our grandparents, it was Pearl Harbor. For our parents, the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. For our generation, it was the terrorist attacks of 9/11. And everyone remembers where they were.
For me, I was in Washington D.C. I was supposed to fly back to Boston on the morning of September 11, but my then-fiancee (and now wife), still at Harvard Law School, asked if I might be able to come back a bit early to help with some wedding planning. So I changed my flights and returned on Monday September 10th. I recall flying through a thunderstorm with jarring turbulence. And on 9/11, I was at my desk when I heard the news. Friends and family, who knew I was supposed to be flying, called to check on me.
And while in shock watching the news unfold on TV, I still remember being paralyzed with panic after learning that one of my friends had departed Logan to attend meetings in Los Angeles. A few hours later, his spouse and I shared a moment of sheer joy when we learned his boss, a very wealthy man, had insisted my friend connect via Dallas to save a bit on airfare. Yes, he was LA bound, but no, he wasn't on either of the planes that hit the towers. Other friends and former colleagues from my time on Wall Street, I later learned, were not as lucky. (For another perspective, you might want to watch President George W. Bush's reflections on how he experienced 9/11...link below).
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ea1903c9-33f3-491c-be10-12731a132c9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
As I sit now and reflect on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks, it is becoming painfully obvious that for the younger folks among us, they don't have the visceral connection or reaction to the events the way I do. It's just something they've read about... or maybe heard about from parents or teachers. "Never Forget," we said, and we haven't. But they can't forget memories they never had in the first place.
I do my part to help them understand what happened by recommending the video below produced by ESPN...and if you haven't yet seen it, I recommend you do...it's less than 15 min and is a powerful story of how 9/11 impacted those who lived through that fateful day. I'm going to now add the George Bush interview to my recommendation.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/497be8b0-27ae-4f20-89a2-a4a03eb1f195?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But some day there will be some event that will shape their lives the way 9/11 and Pearl Harbor shaped the lives of those who came before them. Readers of my work know that [I traffic in predictions](https://substack.com/redirect/81fb5b86-4402-4739-802b-f4c1f93c59fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), so here are some guesses as to what that next history-altering, memory-searing event might be:
**World War III.** We were lulled into a false sense of security after the end of the Cold War with dreams of the "end of history," only to have that peace shattered by Osama bin Laden. Could the end of the Global War on Terror be creating a similarly false sense of security? We seem to be sleepwalking through some very precarious, fragile and delicate times...We often focus inward, while dangerous events unfold globally. There's the Ukraine war, the Iran war, China's aggression...any of these could turn into a flashpoint that sets off another world war. (Side note: If you haven't read Barbara Tuchman's _The Guns of August_ , I'd highly encourage you to do so as it's a great read that sheds light on how a few seemingly localized events led to ever escalating conflict and a world war.)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c9a9d617-79b3-4313-a86a-d507a5bf67a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's not forget that Japan was invading its neighbors and Germany was making aggressive moves well before the invasion of Poland and bombing of Pearl Harbor. Could the Ukraine and Iran conflicts be a buildup to something more extreme? What will the ultimate flashpoint be? Will China finally invade Taiwan? Will Russia attack NATO? Will we see the actual use by a Great Power of nuclear weapons? Any of these have the potential to spark another world war.
**Another 9/11.** For all the failures of the Global War on Terror (two lost wars, a divided country, exploding deficits, diminished civil rights, the rise of the surveillance state, etc), we did win one indisputable victory. There hasn't been another attack on the scale of 9/11 on our homeland. But that doesn't mean there won't be. That's the thing about playing defense against terrorists: we have to be right every time; they only have to be right once.
Our enemies are still out there, and they are still trying to hurt us. A potential attack could take many forms that would be far more devastating than flying planes into buildings. For instance, imagine an [EMP (electromagnetic pulse) attack](https://substack.com/redirect/c424c0b7-4f44-46b0-b638-8f8feeadae15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that takes the American electricity grid down for months if not years.A catastrophic strike on our aging and outdated grid would plunge most of the country into darkness, destroy all temperature control systems protecting food and medicine, and bring life to a halt. 9/11 unified America, but today's polarized population is less likely to unify around any such attack. In fact, the event might even generate infighting among Americans, with political consequences that could (over time) be more dire than the attack itself.
* * *
## [How All Technology Could Fail At Once](https://substack.com/redirect/62949487-bce7-4989-bf70-3654d9f357b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| July 13, 2016
[](https://substack.com/redirect/62949487-bce7-4989-bf70-3654d9f357b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[We live in a scary world, where cyber attacks and shootings compete for headlines with pandemics and climate change. The threat landscape is, to put it bluntly, very crowded. Amid this clamor, there's one danger that warrants more attention, as it could shake the very foundations of society.](https://substack.com/redirect/62949487-bce7-4989-bf70-3654d9f357b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story

* * *
**The Second American Civil War.** Given the polarization and divisiveness of our politics, it's fashionable these days to talk about our country lapsing into another civil war. Our elections are hard-fought and closely divided; both parties jockey for every advantage they can. Just as the addition of states and whether they would send pro- or anti-slavery senators to the US Senate led to the Civil War, parties today are fighting over structural advantages to defeat their opponents. Whether undocumented immigrants can vote or be counted in the census, adding justices to the court, eliminating the Electoral College, voter ID requirements, when to stop counting ballots, floating election deadlines, gerrymandered districts, additional states and the accompanying senators...these things go beyond electioneering and persuasion and seek to tilt the playing field one way or the other. It's only a matter of time before such maneuvers go too far and delegitimize our elections. Could it lead to a civil war as political violence is seen as the only path forward?
**AI breaks out.** Artificial intelligence has been dominating the news as of late, and advancements have been simultaneously exciting and scary. No one truly knows what the ultimate impact will be, the heights we could reach, or the risks associated with it. The nightmare scenario would be a superintelligent, self-improving, ever-evolving AI somehow breaking out of its lab confines and running wild upon the world. Would it be benevolent? Or would the system try to help us in ways that we cannot imagine? Or would it declare war on humanity, thinking us beyond redemption or fighting a war for its very survival? Regardless, its impact would be earth-shattering and era-defining.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5fe23414-ab71-4d1b-9285-97db7c0e06d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
With our 250th birthday behind us, we can still look out upon the world and know that we are the richest and most powerful country in history, confident that any challengers can be rebuffed. Of course, there was a time when the Romans and the British could do the same, and we are all painfully aware that the lessons of history teach that empires never last forever. Will the 21st century witness the decline of American dominance? Any of the scenarios above could very well bring it about.
[CLICK TO READ MY ANNUAL PREDICTIONS](https://substack.com/redirect/81fb5b86-4402-4739-802b-f4c1f93c59fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Readers will know that I don't offer predictions with an objective of accuracy. Instead, I measure the value of the predictions by their usefulness. Do they help us think differently? Can they help us navigate an uncertain world? I don't know which of these, if any, will be the defining moment for the next generation. Nobody does. But I do know that the world is not getting safer, that the risks are not diminishing, and that the sense of invulnerability that preceded both Pearl Harbor and 9/11 is the most dangerous condition of all.
The best we can do is what we've always done: stay vigilant, think clearly, prepare for the scenarios we'd rather not imagine, and never assume that the peace and prosperity we enjoy today is permanent. Twenty-five years ago, on a clear September morning, we learned that lesson the hardest way possible. The question is whether we still remember it.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139121498/646302501/1239926708?refcode=ea.de3fb632-8caf-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ms=ea.de3fb632-8caf-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZTNmYjYzMi04Y2FmLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dBJoYC5Y8_OvrD0s6y5h-vWUuWfx9q7TLTlhlVUHBGU=&emci=c186146f-05ae-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=de3fb632-8caf-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=51844520) Today is Grandparents Day, and I am thinking about my Bubby. She came here with my newborn mom after they were both liberated by U.S. Army soldiers from Buchenwald, a Nazi concentration camp. Both of them instilled in me a deep appreciation for our American values of freedom and opportunity for all. I have always been profoundly inspired by their stories and their commitment to believing in a better future. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139121499/646302504/-223779396?refcode=ea.de3fb632-8caf-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ms=ea.de3fb632-8caf-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZTNmYjYzMi04Y2FmLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dBJoYC5Y8_OvrD0s6y5h-vWUuWfx9q7TLTlhlVUHBGU=)
_(Yes, that baby is me!)_ Learning about my family's story was what first drove me to commit my life to public service. Since then, I've dedicated my career to ensuring that all people — no matter their gender, ethnicity, faith, or who they love — are free from discrimination, hatred, and oppression. **I will be a governor for _all_ Coloradans, because I believe _all_ of us deserve the kind of opportunity this country showed my grandparents and my mother when they first arrived here as refugees.** None of us deserve to live in fear of our rights and freedoms being stripped away by the lawless bullies in the Trump administration. None of us ought to worry about making ends meet, finding housing we can afford, or seeing a doctor. And not a single one of us should have to watch our kids leave the state they were raised in, just because they don't have a shot at building a life here. _I say, it's time to stand up and fight like hell for our futures, our kids, and our values._ **[Thanks to my Bubby, I am grateful to know firsthand the promise of America. And, as Colorado's next governor, I will work every single day to uphold our ideals of liberty and justice for all. clean_body: Today is Grandparents Day, and I am thinking about my Bubby. She came here with my newborn mom after they were both liberated by U.S. Army soldiers from Buchenwald, a Nazi concentration camp. Both of them instilled in me a deep appreciation for our American values of freedom and opportunity for all. I have always been profoundly inspired by their stories and their commitment to believing in a better future. = (Yes, that baby is me!) Learning about my family's story was what first drove me to commit my life to public service. Since then, I've dedicated my career to ensuring that all people — no matter their gender, ethnicity, faith, or who they love — are free from discrimination, hatred, and oppression. I will be a governor for all Coloradans, because I believe all of us deserve the kind of opportunity this country showed my grandparents and my mother when they first arrived here as refugees. None of us deserve to live in fear of our rights and freedoms being stripped away by the lawless bullies in the Trump administration. None of us ought to worry about making ends meet, finding housing we can afford, or seeing a doctor. And not a single one of us should have to watch our kids leave the state they were raised in, just because they don't have a shot at building a life here. I say, it's time to stand up and fight like hell for our futures, our kids, and our values. = | | = | = With gratitude, Phil = | Make sure this email goes to your inbox. # [I Keep Having the Same Conversation With Voters Because They Don’t Know Who John Joyce Is.](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/09/13/i-keep-having-the-same-conversation-with-voters-because-they-dont-know-who-john-joyce-is/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)
---
By **Elizabeth Farnham** on September 13, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 09.13.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=c7f15eac37b5614279c4bc1b5ec8f661008f2226ba56455943001665ba45bc08&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8966&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=483004375bbb6a665261e84787295247&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=7510efab0dd136c0c7a183002d740a58)**
---
| **My Most Frequent Conversation With Voters**
---
| |
---
Fairgoer: Who are you running against?
---
Me: Our current U.S. Representative.
---
Fairgoer: Who’s that?
---
And that, Neighbors, is the conversation I hold the most with constituents of multimillionaire John Joyce.
---
Voters don’t know our current U.S. Representative because he hides from us.
---
He doesn’t hold Town Halls to tell us about his terrible votes or our stunningly beautiful Congressional District.
---
He doesn’t debate me to defend his terrible votes and philosophies.
---
He doesn’t pitch his tent at local fairs and festivals to speak with voters.
---
He doesn’t help the poor, or answer your phone calls.
---
He doesn’t write back about the issues you’ve written to him about.
---
He doesn’t criticize Trump for violating human rights and constitutional law.
---
He doesn’t believe in unionized workers.
---
In short, Joyce doesn’t do anything for Everyday Americans.
---
He only admires Trump.
---
So don’t vote for him in November.
---
Vote for me, Beth Farnham, to actually represent us.
---
We may not agree on everything, but you know I’ll show up for you because I do all of those things.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and vote out the do-nothing.
---
| **Labor Day is for Workers**
---
| |
---
This Labor Day, I spoke with voters in Juniata County, including this family giving away produce on my way to the Juniata County Fair whose local small business is the [Electric Sign Company](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=83ee758c89abe4b35ce4d6b6805a615b4dc79cfd2d6621721e1325ea593ad4f6&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8966&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=31742d9876b59b508484604c0db6f109&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZmFjZWJvb2suY29tL3AvRWxlY3RyaWMtU2lnbi1Db21wYW55LTYxNTkzODU0MzAwMzY5Lw=&email_id=7510efab0dd136c0c7a183002d740a58).
---
Many thanks to the Juniata County Democratic Committee who hosted me at their table on Monday. I spoke with so many people about the current threats to our national security, the unaffordability of our everyday essentials, and our voting rights under siege.
---
Everyday Americans are ready to take our country back from the ultra-wealthy and their cronies in Congress like our own US Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce. Today was a wonderful reminder of the marching generations who fought for livable wages and better working conditions that we enjoy today.
---
I am proud to be endorsed by the United Mine Workers of America, the National Education Association, the Pennsylvania State Education Association, the Pennsylvania Machinists Union, the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO, and the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers.
---
I will continue their fights for a liveable federal minimum wage, a national healthcare plan, scrapping the cap of the social security contributions, the PRO Act, the Faster Labor Contracts Act, and more.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and Working Families!
---
| | **Remembering September 11th**
---
| | |
---|---|---
|
---|---
As the nation mourned the Americans killed in the 9/11 terrorist attack 25 years ago on Friday, we reflected on the heros who saved so many lives.
---
Mr. Fred Rogers said, “Look for the helpers,” and they were there in full force – on the streets, in the stairwells, on the water, in the shops, and in the passenger cabin of Flight 93. Many lost their lives in the aftermath and we mourn them too, but because of their efforts, thousands more survived.
---
May we never forget the lives lost to unspeakable violence and the brave response of so many.
---
| |
---
| **Gleaning to Help Hungry Pennsylvanians**
---
| |
---
Many thanks to SCCAP for coordinating a gleaning on Tuesday.
---
I was glad to pick corn for hungry Pennsylvanians though it isn’t really enough as food pantries struggle to keep up to with increasing demand since SNAP benefits were cut by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
---
You see, while elitists like our own US Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce, are sequestering themselves in Trump’s gilded White-House-turned-palace, more and more Pennsylvanians are struggling to afford food.
---
“The majority of [new clients] that we’ve spoken to and asked these questions are people who have had their SNAP either cut or taken away completely,” Eagen said. “Most of them are working, and they just can’t make ends meet between their income and the price of gas.”
---

name: David Hogg
subject: A generational divide?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Our movement has never been about young vs. old.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260913-1&t=1&akid=4001%2E587540%2EZGPJqJ)
Let’s clear the air, Peter.
Too many people think our movement is about young vs. old. It’s not, and it never has been.
Our movement is about helping elect leaders who are actually representative of the voters who put them in office.
Too many politicians in Washington and in state houses across the country are painfully out of touch with the reality their constituents face. While working families are getting crushed by rising costs and corporate greed, politicians are more concerned with keeping their seats and pleasing their mega-donors than delivering actual results.
**_That’s_ the real problem: a lack of action from leaders who answer to corporations and billionaires — not voters. **
And it’s exactly why talented young leaders rarely run for office in the first place. Going up against a deep-pocketed incumbent is intimidating, and the system is designed to keep it that way.
But the number of people who want something different keeps growing every single day, and so does the number of young leaders willing to step up and be bold. It’s clear: they’re done waiting.
Leaders We Deserve exists to back them. We’re supporting fearless progressive leaders in flippable red-to-blue races across the country all cycle long. Not simply because of their age, but because they understand the moral clarity and urgency this moment demands. They’ll go to the mat for working people, because they know exactly what they’re going through.
With roughly 50 days left until the midterms, these are races that will decide whether the GOP keeps squeezing Americans dry, or we finally elect principled leaders to fight for us in the halls of power.
**[If you’re ready to elect the next generation of leaders who are committed to fighting for working people, please pitch in $5 today to help us win these critical races.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260913_1_misunderstood.sD-2Uo&refcode=em20260913-4001&amount=5&t=2&akid=4001%2E587540%2EZGPJqJ)**

subject: WATCH: I flew 800 miles to fact-check a U.S. Senator
body:
A Senator said island voters must fly 800 miles to prove citizenship.
Four government offices said otherwise.

A Senator said island voters must fly 800 miles to prove citizenship.
Four government offices said otherwise.

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6107070/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YveU5qWlJrVjRmSg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MTM/LbmNsQjcwSTBqRQ/qP2hpZHM9bmN5Z0JTUjFZSDZyTTBsc10/gaqbOYQ/sera1ed57a5

[O'Keefe Media Group]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Dear Friend,

My name is JAMES O'KEEFE. For fifteen years I have carried a hidden
camera into places powerful people would rather I stayed out of, and I
want to tell you about the last place it took me.

A United States Senator stood on the Senate floor and MADE A SPECIFIC
CLAIM ABOUT A VERY SMALL ISLAND IN ALASKA.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

She said that if the SAVE Act passes, a fisherman or a teacher living
in UNALASKA would have to fly 800 MILES into Anchorage just to prove
American citizenship. She even attached a price to it: ELEVEN HUNDRED
DOLLARS A SEAT, plus a hotel, cabs and food, which adds up to
thousands of dollars to cast a single vote.
[Donation Page]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

That is a powerful argument. It is exactly the kind of argument that
quietly kills legislation.

Nobody had checked it. So I BOUGHT THE PLANE TICKET. WATCH WHAT I
FOUND, THEN HELP ME BUY THE NEXT ONE.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Unalaska sits out in the Aleutian chain, roughly 800 miles off the
Alaskan coast. A fishing town, a few thousand people, the middle of
absolutely nowhere.

Then I started knocking on doors.

THE LIBRARIAN told me you can register to vote right there at the
library, and present your documentary proof of citizenship right there
as well. They process passport applications, too.

THE DMV, which we did not even know existed on that island, operates
inside the public safety building. Bring two documents and you walk
out with a state ID, and the very same application asks whether you
would like to register to vote.

THE POST OFFICE was blunter than anybody: "EVERYBODY THAT LIVES ON
THIS ISLAND HAS VOTER REGISTRATION CARDS THAT WE SHOW WHEN WE GO
VOTE."

Then THE CITY CLERK, who seemed to be a genuine admirer of the
Senator, confirmed that City Hall remains a polling location even if
the SAVE Act becomes federal law.

FOUR GOVERNMENT OFFICES, FOUR IDENTICAL ANSWERS, AND NOBODY HAS TO FLY
ANYWHERE.

>> WATCH THE FOOTAGE AND CHIP IN $35 <<
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
Then I found the detail I cannot stop thinking about.

Remember the fishermen, the people the Senator said she was standing
up for? I asked a man down at the harbor how many fishermen actually
live in Unalaska. He explained that thousands arrive for the season,
and when the season ends, every one of them goes home.

So I walked over and asked the fishermen myself. One was from HOUSTON.
Three were from CALIFORNIA. One lived in SEATTLE.

NOT A SINGLE ONE OF THEM LIVED ON THAT ISLAND. THIS IS WHAT IT LOOKS
LIKE WHEN SOMEBODY ACTUALLY GOES AND CHECKS.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Before anybody tries to turn this into a party fight, let me say it
plainly. Senator Murkowski is a REPUBLICAN, and it makes no difference
to me whatsoever. I have done this to Democrats, to Republicans, and
to people with no party at all, because THE TRUTH DOES NOT CHECK YOUR
VOTER REGISTRATION FIRST.

Her office responded to our video by saying she stands by her
concerns, and that it "REMAINS UNCLEAR" how these processes would
operate under an entirely new federal requirement.

Unclear. I flew 800 miles and asked four government offices, and the
whole verification took a single afternoon.

Here is what happened next, and it is the reason I am writing to you.

Days earlier, in that same state, I gave the name of the Senator's own
brother at a polling place and said out loud that I HAD NO
IDENTIFICATION ON ME. I was told it was "ABSOLUTELY POSSIBLE" for me
to vote. I DID NOT VOTE. I DID NOT SIGN ANYONE'S NAME. I NEVER TOUCHED
A BALLOT. I asked a question and I recorded the answer.

Her office did not announce an investigation or a correction. Her
office announced that VOTER IMPERSONATION SHOULD BE PROSECUTED TO THE
FULLEST EXTENT OF THE LAW, and her state director is now submitting a
report against one of my journalists to the Division of Elections and
the Department of Law.

Nobody ever rushes to close the hole. THEY COME AFTER THE MAN HOLDING
THE FLASHLIGHT.

>> YES — FUND THE NEXT INVESTIGATION <<
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
So let me be honest with you about what this kind of reporting costs.

The Senator said an Unalaska fisherman would have to spend eleven
hundred dollars on a plane ticket to prove he is an American citizen.
Here is how that turned out: THE ONLY PERSON WHO EVER BOUGHT THAT
TICKET WAS ME.

That is the price of verifying one sentence. The flights, the days on
the ground, the equipment, and the attorney who reviewed every frame
of that footage before it aired.

WE TAKE NO MONEY FROM THE GOVERNMENT. WE ANSWER TO NO CORPORATE OWNER.
THERE IS NO BILLIONAIRE BEHIND ME. Ordinary Americans pay for this
work, one gift at a time, and THAT IS THE ONLY REASON IT EXISTS.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

AMERICA STARTS VOTING SEPTEMBER 19, when the first federal ballots go
out. Every claim we have not checked by then gets voted on anyway.

You cannot fly to Unalaska. I can. That is the arrangement I am
offering you. YOU FUND THE MISSION, MY TEAM CARRIES THE RISK, AND YOU
SEE THE RESULT WITH YOUR OWN EYES.

>> CHIP IN $35 AND FUND THE NEXT FLIGHT <<
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
One more thing, and it genuinely matters.

A federal appeals court in Washington just threw out the jury verdict
against me and ruled that UNDERCOVER REPORTING LIKE OURS IS PROTECTED
BY THE FIRST AMENDMENT. For fifteen years I have been told that what
we do is not really journalism. A court has now said otherwise.

WE WON THE RIGHT TO KEEP GOING. WHAT WE NEED NOW ARE THE MEANS TO GO.

Thank you for all that you do, and please . . . stay tuned.

In Truth,[James O'Keefe]
James O'Keefe
Founder, O'Keefe Media Group

P.S. A United States Senator told the Senate that island voters would
have to fly 800 miles and spend thousands of dollars to prove their
citizenship. The librarian said no. The DMV said no. The post office
said no. The city clerk said no. THAT ENTIRE FACT-CHECK TOOK ONE PLANE
TICKET AND ONE HONEST QUESTION, AND TICKETS LIKE THAT ARE BOUGHT BY
PEOPLE LIKE YOU.

THE POST OFFICE was blunter than anybody: "EVERYBODY THAT LIVES ON THIS ISLAND HAS VOTER REGISTRATION CARDS THAT WE SHOW WHEN WE GO VOTE." Then THE CITY CLERK, who seemed to be a genuine admirer of the Senator, confirmed that City Hall remains a polling location even if the SAVE Act becomes federal law. FOUR GOVERNMENT OFFICES, FOUR IDENTICAL ANSWERS, AND NOBODY HAS TO FLY ANYWHERE. > WATCH THE FOOTAGE AND CHIP IN $35 << [ Then I found the detail I cannot stop thinking about. Remember the fishermen, the people the Senator said she was standing up for? I asked a man down at the harbor how many fishermen actually live in Unalaska. He explained that thousands arrive for the season, and when the season ends, every one of them goes home. So I walked over and asked the fishermen myself. One was from HOUSTON. Three were from CALIFORNIA. One lived in SEATTLE. NOT A SINGLE ONE OF THEM LIVED ON THAT ISLAND. THIS IS WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE WHEN SOMEBODY ACTUALLY GOES AND CHECKS. [ Before anybody tries to turn this into a party fight, let me say it plainly. Senator Murkowski is a REPUBLICAN, and it makes no difference to me whatsoever. I have done this to Democrats, to Republicans, and to people with no party at all, because THE TRUTH DOES NOT CHECK YOUR VOTER REGISTRATION FIRST. Her office responded to our video by saying she stands by her concerns, and that it "REMAINS UNCLEAR" how these processes would operate under an entirely new federal requirement. Unclear. I flew 800 miles and asked four government offices, and the whole verification took a single afternoon. Here is what happened next, and it is the reason I am writing to you. Days earlier, in that same state, I gave the name of the Senator's own brother at a polling place and said out loud that I HAD NO IDENTIFICATION ON ME. I was told it was "ABSOLUTELY POSSIBLE" for me to vote. I DID NOT VOTE. I DID NOT SIGN ANYONE'S NAME. I NEVER TOUCHED A BALLOT. I asked a question and I recorded the answer. Her office did not announce an investigation or a correction. Her office announced that VOTER IMPERSONATION SHOULD BE PROSECUTED TO THE FULLEST EXTENT OF THE LAW, and her state director is now submitting a report against one of my journalists to the Division of Elections and the Department of Law. Nobody ever rushes to close the hole. THEY COME AFTER THE MAN HOLDING THE FLASHLIGHT. > YES — FUND THE NEXT INVESTIGATION << [ So let me be honest with you about what this kind of reporting costs. The Senator said an Unalaska fisherman would have to spend eleven hundred dollars on a plane ticket to prove he is an American citizen. Here is how that turned out: THE ONLY PERSON WHO EVER BOUGHT THAT TICKET WAS ME. That is the price of verifying one sentence. The flights, the days on the ground, the equipment, and the attorney who reviewed every frame of that footage before it aired. WE TAKE NO MONEY FROM THE GOVERNMENT. WE ANSWER TO NO CORPORATE OWNER. THERE IS NO BILLIONAIRE BEHIND ME. Ordinary Americans pay for this work, one gift at a time, and THAT IS THE ONLY REASON IT EXISTS. [ AMERICA STARTS VOTING SEPTEMBER 19, when the first federal ballots go out. Every claim we have not checked by then gets voted on anyway. You cannot fly to Unalaska. I can. That is the arrangement I am offering you. YOU FUND THE MISSION, MY TEAM CARRIES THE RISK, AND YOU SEE THE RESULT WITH YOUR OWN EYES. > CHIP IN $35 AND FUND THE NEXT FLIGHT << [ One more thing, and it genuinely matters. A federal appeals court in Washington just threw out the jury verdict against me and ruled that UNDERCOVER REPORTING LIKE OURS IS PROTECTED BY THE FIRST AMENDMENT. For fifteen years I have been told that what we do is not really journalism. A court has now said otherwise. WE WON THE RIGHT TO KEEP GOING. WHAT WE NEED NOW ARE THE MEANS TO GO. Thank you for all that you do, and please . . . stay tuned. In Truth,[James O'Keefe] James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group P.S. The Verdict: Paul Richard Randall, 67, of Orange, was sentenced in August 2026 to 30 years in federal prison -- the statutory maximum -- and ordered to pay $178,746,556.22 in restitution. He pleaded guilty in April 2026 to one count of wire fraud committed while on release in a separate federal case, and has been in custody since June 2025.
The Scheme. Between May 2022 and April 2023 -- roughly 11 months -- Randall and co-conspirators (from Moreno Valley and West Hills) ran a pharmacy called Monte Vista and submitted nearly $270 million in claims to Medi-Cal, the state's Medicaid program. More than $178 million was actually paid out. The method: billing tens of millions of dollars per month for high-reimbursement, non-contracted drugs built from cheap generic ingredients -- medications that were not medically necessary and, in many cases, never delivered to any patient. Court filings cite items like Folite, an over-the-counter folic acid vitamin, billed as pain therapy, and a generic pain medication costing about $5 billed at $13,424. Proceeds were laundered and kickbacks paid through layered third-party transfers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a7b0594f-2dc7-4dc9-b817-5adb44224dc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The open door. This is the part prosecutors themselves confirmed: the scheme "exploited a temporary change in Medi-Cal's prescription drug reimbursement system." The state had suspended prior-authorization requirements -- a control meant to verify that a prescribed drug was necessary and actually dispensed. During that window, the pharmacy was an unchecked billing pipe. A repeat fraudster -- Justice officials described Randall exactly that way -- needed no sophistication, only timing: one count of wire fraud, 11 months, a quarter of a billion dollars.
Recovery math. The plea required forfeiture of accounts exceeding $17 million, three vehicles, seven properties, and sports memorabilia. To date, the government has seized about $126.5 million from Randall and his co-conspirators -- against a $178.7 million restitution order. The gap is real, and no sentence recovers the program funds already spent.
Findings.
1\. Speed of loss exceeded speed of detection. $270 million in false claims flowed through a single pharmacy in under a year; the payout rate -- roughly $16 million per month -- should have triggered utilization alarms far sooner.
2\. Suspension of prior authorization created an unmonitored corridor for high-reimbursement, non-contracted drugs. Controls removed for administrative convenience are exactly where fraud nests.
3\. Recidivism risk was live. Randall committed this while on release in another federal case -- an aggravating factor courts weighed in imposing the maximum.
4\. Maximum sentence, partial recovery. Deterrence landed; the taxpayer hole remains.
Fraud in a program like Medi-Cal doesn't stay contained to the program -- the costs leak into everyone's bills.
Start with the direct hit: when nearly $178 million in bogus payments goes out the door, that money comes from taxpayers, which means higher taxes, cuts elsewhere, or borrowing -- three versions of the same wallet. But the indirect hit is where prices for the rest of us move. Every claim the system pays becomes pricing data. When a $5 generic gets reimbursed at $13,424 and nobody stops it, that inflated number flows into the benchmarks, utilization reports, and reimbursement schedules that private insurers, pharmacy benefit managers, and employers consult when setting their own drug rates and premiums.
Fraud, in other words, poisons the ruler everyone measures with. Insurers anticipating losses -- Medicare and Medicaid programs report tens of billions in improper payments nationally every year -- build a cushion into the premiums they charge employers, and employers pass that cushion into the cost of your health plan, your paycheck, and the price of whatever the company sells.
Then there's the second-order squeeze: once the fraud is exposed, the fix is tighter controls and tighter reimbursement rates, which honest pharmacies and providers -- the ones who never stole a dime -- absorb as lower margins and more paperwork, and some respond by leaving the program entirely, shrinking access for the patients it was built to serve. So the $270 million in claims wasn't stolen from an abstraction; it was stolen from a shared pool, and when the pool runs short, the bill gets split -- through taxes, premiums, and prices -- among everyone who was playing by the rules.
Bottom line: The conviction proves enforcement works. The mechanics prove oversight didn't. Lock the vault means restoring authorization gates, real-time billing thresholds, and pharmacy utilization audits -- before the next 11 months begin.
(Sources: U.S. DOJ press releases, April and August 2026; Press-Enterprise, KTLA, NewsNation coverage.)

DOJ announcements, $178,746,556.22 in restitution and California press coverage | | | Sep 13 | | | | | | | | | | | | The Verdict: Paul Richard Randall, 67, of Orange, was sentenced in August 2026 to 30 years in federal prison -- the statutory maximum -- and ordered to pay $178,746,556.22 in restitution. He pleaded guilty in April 2026 to one count of wire fraud committed while on release in a separate federal case, and has been in custody since June 2025. The Scheme. Between May 2022 and April 2023 -- roughly 11 months -- Randall and co-conspirators (from Moreno Valley and West Hills) ran a pharmacy called Monte Vista and submitted nearly $270 million in claims to Medi-Cal, the state's Medicaid program. More than $178 million was actually paid out. The method: billing tens of millions of dollars per month for high-reimbursement, non-contracted drugs built from cheap generic ingredients -- medications that were not medically necessary and, in many cases, never delivered to any patient. Court filings cite items like Folite, an over-the-counter folic acid vitamin, billed as pain therapy, and a generic pain medication costing about $5 billed at $13,424. Proceeds were laundered and kickbacks paid through layered third-party transfers. | | ---|---|--- The open door. This is the part prosecutors themselves confirmed: the scheme "exploited a temporary change in Medi-Cal's prescription drug reimbursement system." The state had suspended prior-authorization requirements -- a control meant to verify that a prescribed drug was necessary and actually dispensed. During that window, the pharmacy was an unchecked billing pipe. A repeat fraudster -- Justice officials described Randall exactly that way -- needed no sophistication, only timing: one count of wire fraud, 11 months, a quarter of a billion dollars. Recovery math. The plea required forfeiture of accounts exceeding $17 million, three vehicles, seven properties, and sports memorabilia. To date, the government has seized about $126.5 million from Randall and his co-conspirators -- against a $178.7 million restitution order. The gap is real, and no sentence recovers the program funds already spent. Findings. 1\. Speed of loss exceeded speed of detection. $270 million in false claims flowed through a single pharmacy in under a year; the payout rate -- roughly $16 million per month -- should have triggered utilization alarms far sooner. 2\. Suspension of prior authorization created an unmonitored corridor for high-reimbursement, non-contracted drugs. Controls removed for administrative convenience are exactly where fraud nests. 3\. Recidivism risk was live. Randall committed this while on release in another federal case -- an aggravating factor courts weighed in imposing the maximum. 4\. Maximum sentence, partial recovery. Deterrence landed; the taxpayer hole remains. Fraud in a program like Medi-Cal doesn't stay contained to the program -- the costs leak into everyone's bills. Start with the direct hit: when nearly $178 million in bogus payments goes out the door, that money comes from taxpayers, which means higher taxes, cuts elsewhere, or borrowing -- three versions of the same wallet. But the indirect hit is where prices for the rest of us move. Every claim the system pays becomes pricing data. When a $5 generic gets reimbursed at $13,424 and nobody stops it, that inflated number flows into the benchmarks, utilization reports, and reimbursement schedules that private insurers, pharmacy benefit managers, and employers consult when setting their own drug rates and premiums. Fraud, in other words, poisons the ruler everyone measures with. Insurers anticipating losses -- Medicare and Medicaid programs report tens of billions in improper payments nationally every year -- build a cushion into the premiums they charge employers, and employers pass that cushion into the cost of your health plan, your paycheck, and the price of whatever the company sells. Then there's the second-order squeeze: once the fraud is exposed, the fix is tighter controls and tighter reimbursement rates, which honest pharmacies and providers -- the ones who never stole a dime -- absorb as lower margins and more paperwork, and some respond by leaving the program entirely, shrinking access for the patients it was built to serve. So the $270 million in claims wasn't stolen from an abstraction; it was stolen from a shared pool, and when the pool runs short, the bill gets split -- through taxes, premiums, and prices -- among everyone who was playing by the rules. Bottom line: The conviction proves enforcement works. The mechanics prove oversight didn't. Lock the vault means restoring authorization gates, real-time billing thresholds, and pharmacy utilization audits -- before the next 11 months begin. (Sources: U.S. DOJ press releases, April and August 2026; Press-Enterprise, KTLA, NewsNation coverage.) Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. subject: Why you should pay attention to the Michigan Democratic State Party
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
We’ve partnered with Michigan Democrats to run Ground Truth canvasses
#
Hi there,
This year, Swing Left has been working closely with a set of forward-thinking State Democratic Parties to help strengthen infrastructure to sustain Democratic wins for years to come. Today, we want to highlight that work happening in Michigan.
One of those is the Michigan Democratic Party and Coordinated Campaign, where we are scaling **Ground Truth,** our volunteer-led deep-canvassing program that aims to rebuild trust and net votes in critical swing races across the country.
Statewide organizing in Michigan is especially critical right now. Michigan is a must-win battleground state with a massive set of high-stakes races on the ballot this fall. Historically, this state is extremely competitive—an area political analysts often call a purple state. In 2024, Donald Trump won Michigan with 49.7% of the vote; Harris, 48.3%.
We need to defend the open Governor’s mansion, flip the state House while protecting the state Senate majority, win four U.S. House swing seats, and hold one of the most competitive Senate races in the country following Democratic Senator Gary Peters' retirement.
The Michigan State Party and Coordinated Campaign play an integral role in the field program for these races, and resources invested here will help ensure the data they receive from Ground Truth conversations can be put to use across the contests we need to win this year and build ground for 2028.
Swing Left volunteers are helping by conducting Ground Truth canvasses on the ground in Michigan—holding deep, genuine conversations at the doors to address the issues that matter most to voters and gather insights that are made available to the Coordinated Campaign, State Party, and candidates for use in their campaign messaging and strategy.
Working together ensures we’re as efficient as possible in scaling these efforts—and gives the Michigan Democratic Party additional resources to cover more ground alongside Swing Left volunteers in Michigan.
[**That’s why we’re asking you to split a donation between the Michigan Democratic Party and Swing Left today.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl-michiganstateparty.3Bx3tp&refcode=em20260913-2760&amount=25&t=1&akid=2760%2E1562180%2EEkWcVD)
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl-michiganstateparty.3Bx3tp&refcode=em20260913-2760&t=2&akid=2760%2E1562180%2EEkWcVD)**
Donating today will help the state party provide the permanent infrastructure, voter data, and organizing staff that supports candidates up and down the ballot. And a strong state party infrastructure means candidates and campaigns have a foundation to build on instead of starting from scratch every election.
With only 51 days left until Election Day, your support today will help expand Ground Truth canvasses into purple areas across Michigan and ensure candidates in our target races have the resources to win.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260913-1&t=3&refcode2=2760_1562180_EkWcVD&akid=2760%2E1562180%2EEkWcVD)

subject: I want to share something deeply personal with you today.

body:
I've written it all out in a full personal note. I hope you'll take a few minutes to read it.

| |
---
| | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2O2zAQxfHTUB0Ffsi0VKgIYAhIsWm2SCmMyZE0CEUS5Hid4wcqcoG9wA_v_X9_rB9AkdL-C06cqbW1tpXekJhzO6BiyyfyQWkPiGU1yjipJqntCp7pC9cBujDfjB63scNZ38fJ6vtkVHfMRnmn7gBTeA7OW1AepmlAB9qPCu3Y0Xx5atJWu-GmXW9BmZsdxqcewXi9iUG9SgDGnlKjgM3nXEqOxORbn-vexflgLk3YH8IswiwN_ati_6ZUMfQ-n8Iszwop5CR3ilFuuUrGv9CEWQIlbEekDSMllIn2g5-45Yox-z8YJJ6ywAXbpV5wpbQL--D6QmHci8-VvbCPn5-f8v8TYRycXHIjppyEfeiuzqG8KUZq7i4GtZ9A8ZrW8TeDf83mXwAAAP__i1CSnw)
---
Patriot, it's Dinesh D'Souza.

I want to share something deeply personal with you today. Something I've never said quite this way before.

**The night before I was set to be locked away, I made a decision that changed everything about how I fight and how I've fought ever since.**

I'm not going to bury the lead: _**what I learned in that moment is the same thing I believe every patriot in this movement needs to hear right now. **_

Because what we're facing today is a threat to everything we've built — it can feel like the walls are closing in.

I know that feeling.

**And what I learned on the other side of it is something I've passed on to only a handful of people I trust most, including my son-in-law Brandon Gill who took it to Dartmouth, then took it to Washington, and uses it every single day to expose and dismantle the radical left in ways they never saw coming!**

[_**I'm sharing it with you now because I think you need it.**_](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2O2zAQxfHTUB0Ffsi0VKgIYAhIsWm2SCmMyZE0CEUS5Hid4wcqcoG9wA_v_X9_rB9AkdL-C06cqbW1tpXekJhzO6BiyyfyQWkPiGU1yjipJqntCp7pC9cBujDfjB63scNZ38fJ6vtkVHfMRnmn7gBTeA7OW1AepmlAB9qPCu3Y0Xx5atJWu-GmXW9BmZsdxqcewXi9iUG9SgDGnlKjgM3nXEqOxORbn-vexflgLk3YH8IswiwN_ati_6ZUMfQ-n8Iszwop5CR3ilFuuUrGv9CEWQIlbEekDSMllIn2g5-45Yox-z8YJJ6ywAXbpV5wpbQL--D6QmHci8-VvbCPn5-f8v8TYRycXHIjppyEfeiuzqG8KUZq7i4GtZ9A8ZrW8TeDf83mXwAAAP__i1CSnw)

Don’t look at this as another fundraising pitch or one of those doomsday warnings.

body:
It all started in a small town in Aroostook County.
| Hi, it's Susan.I don't get to slow down and share this very often, so today I wanted to take a moment to tell you a bit about how I got here.I grew up in Caribou, Maine - one of six kids raised by my parents, Pat and Don. Both of them served as mayor of Caribou at one point, and my dad, a World War II veteran, went on to serve in the Maine Legislature. Public service just runs in the family - I'm actually the fourth generation of Collins' in public service.Our family also ran a small retail lumber business that's been passed down for six generations, dating back to 1844. Growing up around that kind of hard work taught me a lot about what it means to show up for your community, day after day.My path to Washington wasn't a straight line. I got my start working for a Maine congressman, followed him to the Senate, and eventually found myself championing small businesses - first at the state level, then with the Small Business Administration, and later running a center dedicated to family businesses.Eventually, I ran for the Senate myself, and I've been honored to serve Maine ever since - always trying to work across the aisle and get real results for the people back home.That's my story. Public service just runs in the family - I'm actually the fourth generation of Collins' in public service.Our family also ran a small retail lumber business that's been passed down for six generations, dating back to 1844. Growing up around that kind of hard work taught me a lot about what it means to show up for your community, day after day.My path to Washington wasn't a straight line. I got my start working for a Maine congressman, followed him to the Senate, and eventually found myself championing small businesses - first at the state level, then with the Small Business Administration, and later running a center dedicated to family businesses.Eventually, I ran for the Senate myself, and I've been honored to serve Maine ever since - always trying to work across the aisle and get real results for the people back home.That's my story. Aroostook County roots, a family that believed in service, and a lot of hard work along the way. | Warmly, Susan | The latest numbers out of Maine show Troy Jackson leading by 2 points.We've seen tight races like this before, and we know exactly what it takes to win them. This is the moment to step up, show our strength, and make sure everyone knows we aren't backing down. | Collins is locked in the most fiercely contested race in the entire nation, and everyone - Republicans, Independents, and Democrats alike - is watching desperately to see what happens next.Right now, the Radical Left is flooding the state with resources. If we don't fight back immediately, we risk losing the single most critical seat holding our Senate majority together. We cannot allow outside forces to flip this stronghold. | Paid for by Collins for Senator P.O. Box 1096 Bangor, ME 04402

## **AI Companies Can Slow Down If They Wanted To**
Jacob Coxon's resignation from Anthropic blew up this week. The post you've probably seen has nearly 170 million impressions. Coxon says he spent three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI and Anthropic, and he accused both companies of racing toward self-improving superintelligence and "gambling with our lives."
[| | | | | Jacob Coxon
---
@hilbertspaess
I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. More thoughts below.
| 12:04 AM * Sep 9, 2026 * 169M Views19.9K Replies * 164K Reposts * 791K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/214b6206-a15e-490c-acd4-8030d5560d9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
There is always a possibility that a technology goes wrong. But I am not convinced that the catastrophic future being described is where we are right now, and I am especially skeptical of what the companies building this technology want the government to do about it.
My concern is **[regulatory capture](https://substack.com/redirect/57fabf92-f2ed-4512-a652-f784e62cf67a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. I suspect the biggest companies see an opportunity to use fear to help build a system that protects their position, limits competition and makes it harder for open-source alternatives to survive.
That is not just about money. It is about political power, access to technology and control over the infrastructure everybody else would depend on. If only a couple of companies get to supply the most capable systems, they would have enormous influence over businesses, governments and the public.
David Sacks made the point I keep coming back to: if these companies believe their own products are becoming too dangerous, they can slow down themselves. They don't need the government to tell them what to do.
As he put it:
> "The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it."
Maybe they have built something that genuinely scares them. Fine. Then limit it. Stop the training run. Delay the release. You control your own product.
[| | | | | David Sacks
---
@DavidSacks
Dario has written that we need to "pace the frontier," and Sam has agreed. People may be surprised by my response: go ahead. You guys are the frontier. By any reasonable metric -- market share, revenue growth, model capability -- the two of you have a duopoly on frontier...
| 3:14 AM * Sep 13, 2026 * 132K Views329 Replies * 676 Reposts * 4.12K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/ad15f436-6d95-46a5-ac1a-65f1ecc9cb95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It would be like Apple warning everybody that putting a fourth camera on an iPhone could be dangerous, then demanding a new regulatory system before agreeing not to install it. Just don't put another camera on the phone.
**I do not see why accepting a company 's preferred regulatory framework should become the price of that company acting responsibly.** That is what makes me suspicious.
I also want people to remember the other side of this. If this technology becomes as powerful and economically important as its developers claim, falling behind would carry serious consequences too. I do not want fear to become the justification for giving a handful of companies permanent control over who gets to build and use it.
I'm working on more about historical technology panics. We have plenty of frightening images in our heads, from _The Terminator_ to HAL 9000. But a frightening future scenario is not the same thing as proof that we should hand the companies describing it the power to write the rules.

## **Anonymity for Jurors is Paramount**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a11475aa-ef31-4d9d-8d57-c4c634fb8e80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The media scrutiny of the holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy's trial bothers me. My concern is what happens to jury independence when disagreeing with the other jurors means becoming the next person whose life gets picked apart in public.
I am not asking whether you like his position. I am not asking whether you believe Clancy should have been convicted or acquitted. I am asking what message this sends to the next person sitting in a jury box. Or even if we can get anyone to sit in that box again? OR, if we do get people to sit in the juror's box, then what kind of people are they considering they now will have to be masochistic.
We expect jurors to decide a case based on the evidence and the judge's instructions. We tell them not to research the case, follow the coverage or let outside opinions influence them. Then, after a controversial outcome, we have jurors giving interviews about deliberations while the person who disagreed becomes the focus of another round of coverage.
Massachusetts's own Trial Juror's Handbook says dismissed jurors may discuss their service, but advises them to avoid revealing other jurors' names, their votes or what was discussed during deliberations. That speaks directly to the concern I am raising.
My criticism is also about the media's business model. I think the incentive is to keep the story going. A guilty verdict can generate attention. An acquittal can generate attention. A deadlocked jury and a fight among jurors can generate even more. I worry that protecting the jury process becomes secondary to finding the next clickable development.
I posted that concern on Facebook, and the comment breakdown was interesting.
The comments supporting my concern generally described the scrutiny as unfair, intimidating or potentially harmful to future jurors. Those defending it pointed to questions about the juror's questionnaire, past allegations or whether he followed the law.

## **Watch Yemen and the Expanding Pressure on Energy**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c90a5779-8456-4b60-a781-5c844ed760b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/11/houthi-advance-in-yemen-is-about-more-than-just-the-red-sea](https://substack.com/redirect/205a329c-285b-44e0-bd29-64ae632ad7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Houthi advances within Yemen are another thing I'm watching. I believe we may already be in a wider war , maybe a world war, that is developing gradually, simmering and expanding instead of arriving as one clearly defined event.
What concerns me is how an economic shock or an energy crisis could push things further.
Reuters reported new attacks affecting Saudi oil infrastructure and regional shipping, alongside the Houthi capture of Perim Island near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. These are developments around routes that matter to the movement of energy and goods.
The combination of fighting, damaged infrastructure and pressure on shipping is worth paying attention to.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/fcf3fa67-f84c-4668-84fa-0c66e350aca2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
My concern is that we keep watching these developments individually while the overall situation becomes more dangerous. I think an energy or economic crisis could become the catalyst for something much bigger.
**The Iran conflict, Israel/Gaza, Russia/Ukraine are all part of the same geopolitical conflict even if doesn 't appear to be on the surface.** China, North Korea, South Korea, are involved too even though we do not hear much about them. The sharing of intelligence and arms movement between nations points to something bigger is brewing. Oh, not to mention the frothy stock market, and the surging bond market.

## **Amy Acton and the Canfield Fair Coverage**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/962f4baf-302f-4c63-a3b2-0a30776002f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Moving to Ohio, Amy Acton continues to disappoint me.
An legally armed person charging toward a candidate is an alarming description. Of course people were concerned. But the sheriff's office said the weapons were never brandished or removed from their holsters. Later, a prosecutor said the man wanted to ask Acton questions and was recording, which the Acton campaign said he was not allowed to do (weird and really shitty). Authorities found no threats on his cellphone.
It was also alleged that he knocked people down and caused injuries. The video doesn't show that. I am waiting for more video and hopefully one from his angle.

He pleaded not guilty to charges including assault, disorderly conduct and inducing panic. Carrying weapons, brandishing them and intending to attack a candidate are different things.

This whole incident, in my opinion, is a cover-up for the horrible display onstage with her and Pete Buttigieg. The negative press surrounding that speech quickly faded as the campaign and media overamplified an incident involving someone who wanted access. The fact that they said "no cameras" while she was campaigning is absolutely crazy and, in my opinion, should be considered a violation of the basic expectations of campaigning.
My broader frustration is with access. If you are walking around in public with a campaign staff wearing your name, questions, comments and pictures are part of what you are there to do.
I want candidates to be accessible. I want them answering questions, including questions they do not particularly like.
Democrats cannot keep saying we want openness and communication while becoming defensive whenever that access something we don't like. I criticized the same tendency around **Chris Ronayne,** and I am not going to stop criticizing it because another Democrat is involved.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3689dbd4-d5a2-4e6d-98bd-22a4a58e21ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

## **Chris Ronayne 's Spend Spend Spend**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/de7efbb8-d73e-4fb6-a508-e40d2dabd0f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That brings me to Chris Ronayne and the county's finances.
His State of the County address laid out a vision for growth and prosperity. But according to News 5, the speech did not directly address the county's significant budget problems. The report identified a projected **$19 million general-fund deficit** and an **$18 million shortfall in the Health and Human Services levy fund**.
The county is seeking 3.3 percent spending reductions from general-fund departments and 8 percent reductions in 2027 spending from departments supported by the HHS levy. Ronayne said the HHS cuts would be rolled back if voters approved the November levy. Sounds like extortion to me.
A small-business owner asked him to pledge against supporting additional tax increases during his second term.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f45b7680-709c-4ef7-bad1-881f944238a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
His response:
> "I can't pledge to not support any tax increase in the future because I do believe there are things worth paying for."
And that is where the frustration is. People are paying too much for everything right now and big ticket items are being passed by this county council with no accountability and it falls on the people of the county to pay for it. The possibility of another tax increase remains on the table while the county is already dealing with substantial shortfalls. Irresponsible!
Calling something an investment does not make is fiscally responsible. Announcing cuts does not answer the question about how the county got here. Lying to voters then spending billions is, IMO, fraud.
Looking around the audience, I recognized plenty of elected officials and political insiders. The audience seemed to be half filled with his Cuyahoga political buds, all sitting there loving more taxes. That is why these events feel so performative. The people already involved in the political system are there just rubbing each other's rhubarb while the people are not in attendance. The pictures come out to make it look like it is a packed house.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5013cbc8-10f7-437a-9e0d-45c53eb7737f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The public has responsibility here too. We cannot keep leaving these conversations to the same people and then act surprised when they dominate the decisions.
I want less performance, more direct discussion of the bills and more residents showing up before those bills become another tax proposal.
It is also frustrating to see Chris Ronayne block reporters from attending fundraisers, even after they received invitations, while using his own campaign funds and holding fundraisers for candidates who are not speaking out against these budgets. These candidates appear ready to toe the line, abandon fiscal responsibility and serve as rubber stamps for whatever Ronayne wants to do. This is something we must pay attention to.

## **A Quick Note: Brian Poindexter**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5210ba02-97ee-410c-bb38-9a9fee9d446f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

On a more positive note, **Brian Poindexter** has an upcoming fundraiser in Rocky River involving my old friend Michael O'Shea.
I wanted to pass that along because I encourage people to support Brian in his campaign against Max Miller. I have shared the invitation on my page so people can check the event information directly.

## **Apple Finally Folds. I 'm Still Gonna Wait.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/793df017-e343-447d-bf83-3dae81300801?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Finally, something completely different: Apple's new phones.
Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, along with its first folding phone, the **iPhone Duo**. The Pro models are scheduled to become available September 18, while the Duo arrives October 23.
To be perfectly honest, I think the folding phone looks really good.
Apple has often let other companies introduce a product or innovation, and work through some of the awkward early versions before making its own. Samsung and other manufacturers have already spent years refining folding phones, from book-style devices to smaller flip designs. Apple certainly did not rush to be first.
What interests me is whether that patience produces a better first attempt. From the presentation, I think the Duo looks promising. But I still want to see the reviews and hear from people who have actually used it.
That has generally been my attitude toward first-generation Apple products. I can appreciate the idea without wanting to be the person paying to discover all the compromises.
The original Apple Watch interested me, but later versions became just better. I felt similarly about the move from the original iPhone ( which didn't have cope paste functions) to the iPhone 3G. And while I liked the iPhone Air's design, I was less enthusiastic about the trade-offs.
The Pro and Pro Max look like continued refinement of a product Apple already knows how to make very well. That is not as exciting as a phone that folds, but refinement is not a bad thing when you are buying something you use all day.
The Duo looks like a strong first shot. I'm interested. I want to see how it performs. But my instinct is still to wait for gen 2.
Especially when we are talking about roughly $2,000 for a phone. Thats insane. But so is $4.50/gal gas.
