Coxon says he spent three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI and Anthropic, and he accused both companies of racing toward self-improving superintelligence and "gambling with our lives." There is always a possibility that a technology goes wrong. But I am not convinced that the catastrophic future being described is where we are right now, and I am especially skeptical of what the companies building this technology want the government to do about it. My concern is . I suspect the biggest companies see an opportunity to use fear to help build a system that protects their position, limits competition and makes it harder for open-source alternatives to survive. That is not just about money. It is about political power, access to technology and control over the infrastructure everybody else would depend on. If only a couple of companies get to supply the most capable systems, they would have enormous influence over businesses, governments and the public. David Sacks made the point I keep coming back to: if these companies believe their own products are becoming too dangerous, they can slow down themselves. They don't need the government to tell them what to do. As he put it: "The easiest way not to build superintelligence is for you to agree not to build it." Maybe they have built something that genuinely scares them. Fine. Then limit it. Stop the training run. Delay the release. You control your own product. It would be like Apple warning everybody that putting a fourth camera on an iPhone could be dangerous, then demanding a new regulatory system before agreeing not to install it. Just don't put another camera on the phone. I do not see why accepting a company 's preferred regulatory framework should become the price of that company acting responsibly. That is what makes me suspicious. I also want people to remember the other side of this. If this technology becomes as powerful and economically important as its developers claim, falling behind would carry serious consequences too. I do not want fear to become the justification for giving a handful of companies permanent control over who gets to build and use it. I'm working on more about historical technology panics. We have plenty of frightening images in our heads, from The Terminator to HAL 9000. But a frightening future scenario is not the same thing as proof that we should hand the companies describing it the power to write the rules. Anonymity for Jurors is Paramount | | ---|---|--- The media scrutiny of the holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy's trial bothers me. My concern is what happens to jury independence when disagreeing with the other jurors means becoming the next person whose life gets picked apart in public. I am not asking whether you like his position. I am not asking whether you believe Clancy should have been convicted or acquitted. I am asking what message this sends to the next person sitting in a jury box. Or even if we can get anyone to sit in that box again? OR, if we do get people to sit in the juror's box, then what kind of people are they considering they now will have to be masochistic. We expect jurors to decide a case based on the evidence and the judge's instructions. We tell them not to research the case, follow the coverage or let outside opinions influence them. Then, after a controversial outcome, we have jurors giving interviews about deliberations while the person who disagreed becomes the focus of another round of coverage. Massachusetts's own Trial Juror's Handbook says dismissed jurors may discuss their service, but advises them to avoid revealing other jurors' names, their votes or what was discussed during deliberations. That speaks directly to the concern I am raising. My criticism is also about the media's business model. I think the incentive is to keep the story going. A guilty verdict can generate attention. An acquittal can generate attention. A deadlocked jury and a fight among jurors can generate even more. I worry that protecting the jury process becomes secondary to finding the next clickable development. I posted that concern on Facebook, and the comment breakdown was interesting. The comments supporting my concern generally described the scrutiny as unfair, intimidating or potentially harmful to future jurors. Those defending it pointed to questions about the juror's questionnaire, past allegations or whether he followed the law. | | ---|---|--- Watch Yemen and the Expanding Pressure on Energy | | ---|---|--- The Houthi advances within Yemen are another thing I'm watching. I believe we may already be in a wider war , maybe a world war, that is developing gradually, simmering and expanding instead of arriving as one clearly defined event. What concerns me is how an economic shock or an energy crisis could push things further. Reuters reported new attacks affecting Saudi oil infrastructure and regional shipping, alongside the Houthi capture of Perim Island near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. These are developments around routes that matter to the movement of energy and goods. The combination of fighting, damaged infrastructure and pressure on shipping is worth paying attention to. My concern is that we keep watching these developments individually while the overall situation becomes more dangerous. I think an energy or economic crisis could become the catalyst for something much bigger. The Iran conflict, Israel/Gaza, Russia/Ukraine are all part of the same geopolitical conflict even if doesn 't appear to be on the surface. China, North Korea, South Korea, are involved too even though we do not hear much about them. The sharing of intelligence and arms movement between nations points to something bigger is brewing. Oh, not to mention the frothy stock market, and the surging bond market. Amy Acton and the Canfield Fair Coverage Moving to Ohio, Amy Acton continues to disappoint me. An legally armed person charging toward a candidate is an alarming description. Of course people were concerned. But the sheriff's office said the weapons were never brandished or removed from their holsters. Later, a prosecutor said the man wanted to ask Acton questions and was recording, which the Acton campaign said he was not allowed to do (weird and really shitty). Authorities found no threats on his cellphone. It was also alleged that he knocked people down and caused injuries. The video doesn't show that. I am waiting for more video and hopefully one from his angle. He pleaded not guilty to charges including assault, disorderly conduct and inducing panic. Carrying weapons, brandishing them and intending to attack a candidate are different things. This whole incident, in my opinion, is a cover-up for the horrible display onstage with her and Pete Buttigieg. The negative press surrounding that speech quickly faded as the campaign and media overamplified an incident involving someone who wanted access. The fact that they said "no cameras" while she was campaigning is absolutely crazy and, in my opinion, should be considered a violation of the basic expectations of campaigning. My broader frustration is with access. If you are walking around in public with a campaign staff wearing your name, questions, comments and pictures are part of what you are there to do. I want candidates to be accessible. I want them answering questions, including questions they do not particularly like. Democrats cannot keep saying we want openness and communication while becoming defensive whenever that access something we don't like. I criticized the same tendency around Chris Ronayne, and I am not going to stop criticizing it because another Democrat is involved. Chris Ronayne 's Spend Spend Spend | | ---|---|--- That brings me to Chris Ronayne and the county's finances. His State of the County address laid out a vision for growth and prosperity. But according to News 5, the speech did not directly address the county's significant budget problems. The report identified a projected $19 million general-fund deficit and an $18 million shortfall in the Health and Human Services levy fund. The county is seeking 3.3 percent spending reductions from general-fund departments and 8 percent reductions in 2027 spending from departments supported by the HHS levy. Ronayne said the HHS cuts would be rolled back if voters approved the November levy. Sounds like extortion to me. A small-business owner asked him to pledge against supporting additional tax increases during his second term. His response: "I can't pledge to not support any tax increase in the future because I do believe there are things worth paying for." And that is where the frustration is. People are paying too much for everything right now and big ticket items are being passed by this county council with no accountability and it falls on the people of the county to pay for it. The possibility of another tax increase remains on the table while the county is already dealing with substantial shortfalls. Irresponsible! Calling something an investment does not make is fiscally responsible. Announcing cuts does not answer the question about how the county got here. Lying to voters then spending billions is, IMO, fraud. Looking around the audience, I recognized plenty of elected officials and political insiders. The audience seemed to be half filled with his Cuyahoga political buds, all sitting there loving more taxes. That is why these events feel so performative. The people already involved in the political system are there just rubbing each other's rhubarb while the people are not in attendance. The pictures come out to make it look like it is a packed house. The public has responsibility here too. We cannot keep leaving these conversations to the same people and then act surprised when they dominate the decisions. I want less performance, more direct discussion of the bills and more residents showing up before those bills become another tax proposal. It is also frustrating to see Chris Ronayne block reporters from attending fundraisers, even after they received invitations, while using his own campaign funds and holding fundraisers for candidates who are not speaking out against these budgets. These candidates appear ready to toe the line, abandon fiscal responsibility and serve as rubber stamps for whatever Ronayne wants to do. This is something we must pay attention to. A Quick Note: Brian Poindexter | | ---|---|--- On a more positive note, Brian Poindexter has an upcoming fundraiser in Rocky River involving my old friend Michael O'Shea. I wanted to pass that along because I encourage people to support Brian in his campaign against Max Miller. I have shared the invitation on my page so people can check the event information directly. Apple Finally Folds. I 'm Still Gonna Wait. | | ---|---|--- Finally, something completely different: Apple's new phones. Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, along with its first folding phone, the iPhone Duo. The Pro models are scheduled to become available September 18, while the Duo arrives October 23. To be perfectly honest, I think the folding phone looks really good. Apple has often let other companies introduce a product or innovation, and work through some of the awkward early versions before making its own. Samsung and other manufacturers have already spent years refining folding phones, from book-style devices to smaller flip designs. Apple certainly did not rush to be first. What interests me is whether that patience produces a better first attempt. From the presentation, I think the Duo looks promising. But I still want to see the reviews and hear from people who have actually used it. That has generally been my attitude toward first-generation Apple products. I can appreciate the idea without wanting to be the person paying to discover all the compromises. The original Apple Watch interested me, but later versions became just better. I felt similarly about the move from the original iPhone ( which didn't have cope paste functions) to the iPhone 3G. And while I liked the iPhone Air's design, I was less enthusiastic about the trade-offs. The Pro and Pro Max look like continued refinement of a product Apple already knows how to make very well. That is not as exciting as a phone that folds, but refinement is not a bad thing when you are buying something you use all day. The Duo looks like a strong first shot. I'm interested. I want to see how it performs. But my instinct is still to wait for gen 2. Especially when we are talking about roughly $2,000 for a phone. Thats insane. But so is $4.50/gal gas. Stay Angry. name: Cooper, Roy
subject: I knew I had to do something
body:
Folks had placed their trust in me.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1331&source=&t=1&akid=3456%2E124072%2EnsnSxQ) | | | |
---
Peter,

At the end of this message, [**_I’m going to ask you to make your first donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate in North Carolina._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1331&amount=5&t=8&akid=3456%2E124072%2EnsnSxQ) But first, will you let me explain why your support – especially ahead of our mid-month deadline – is so important?
Frankly, running for Senate wasn't part of the plan. I wanted to serve North Carolina from right here at home.

Seeing all of the chaos and horrors coming out of Washington DC, I knew I had to do something. Folks had placed their trust in me throughout my career as a public servant to fight for them – and **I felt that responsibility deeply.**
This is a race I simply could not walk away from. It’s also one I know we can win.

Since launching our campaign, tens of thousands of people have joined our grassroots movement. I’m so grateful to count you as one of them, Peter.
**With a recent poll showing this race statistically tied, and far-right Republicans spending over $100 million to defeat me, I need your help to keep up our momentum.**
[**_I set a goal to raise $2.5 million before our September mid-month deadline, and I’m counting on your support to reach it. Your contribution of $5 will be put to work immediately to help us win in North Carolina and take back the Senate. Will you chip in?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1331&amount=5&t=9&akid=3456%2E124072%2EnsnSxQ)

Roy Cooper

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. When working people organize, powerful people cannot simply make the rules for everyone else. | |

Peter, **There is a reason powerful people have always been afraid of organized workers. When people organize together, we become harder to ignore, harder to divide, and much harder to strip of our power.** On November 3, working people across this country will try to vote while the companies that employ them treat Election Day like any other shift. Walmart, Amazon, Home Depot, Target, Starbucks, Albertsons, and Kroger can give every employee paid time off to vote. **The people who stock the shelves, pack the boxes, ring up groceries, and pour the coffee know what it means to be told there is no time. A conflicting work schedule was the leading reason eligible voters stayed home in the 2022 midterms.** Working people should not lose our voice in our democracy when we clock in for work. The same people who keep these companies running every day should have the time and opportunity to participate in the decisions that shape our communities, our workplaces, and our lives. **This fight is bigger than one company policy. People who want unchecked power depend on working people believing we are powerless.** They benefit when communities are divided, when election denialism makes people doubt that their vote will count, and when voters lose faith that their voices can change anything.
Working people organizing together have won rights that once seemed impossible, built power in communities that politicians ignored, and forced wealthy interests to answer to people they would rather overlook.

clean_body: When working people organize, powerful people cannot simply make the rules for everyone else. | | Peter, There is a reason powerful people have always been afraid of organized workers. When people organize together, we become harder to ignore, harder to divide, and much harder to strip of our power. On November 3, working people across this country will try to vote while the companies that employ them treat Election Day like any other shift. Walmart, Amazon, Home Depot, Target, Starbucks, Albertsons, and Kroger can give every employee paid time off to vote. The people who stock the shelves, pack the boxes, ring up groceries, and pour the coffee know what it means to be told there is no time. A conflicting work schedule was the leading reason eligible voters stayed home in the 2022 midterms. Working people should not lose our voice in our democracy when we clock in for work. The same people who keep these companies running every day should have the time and opportunity to participate in the decisions that shape our communities, our workplaces, and our lives. | | This fight is bigger than one company policy. People who want unchecked power depend on working people believing we are powerless. They benefit when communities are divided, when election denialism makes people doubt that their vote will count, and when voters lose faith that their voices can change anything. Working people organizing together have won rights that once seemed impossible, built power in communities that politicians ignored, and forced wealthy interests to answer to people they would rather overlook. That same organizing power is essential to defending our democracy. I have to be honest with you about what running a campaign feels like from the inside.
It is a giant machine with a thousand moving parts, and most days you are building the plane while flying it.
Managed chaos is the nicest name for it.
But every so often you get handed a simple gift like that text, and it reminds you why we go through all of it.
This campaign, at its heart, is service over self.
And when we knock doors and hold town halls in places extremists like Keith Self stopped visiting years ago, something happens.
People who never joined the political process, or who gave up on it a long time ago, start to believe again.
A first yard sign after seven years is what hope looks like on an ordinary street corner.

They know they do not need to win everywhere. They only need enough close seats to keep Mike Johnson in the Speaker’s chair and keep Trump’s majority alive. That makes this district a direct target. I will not let DC insiders decide who represents us. This seat belongs to the people who live here—not Donald Trump, party bosses, or the biggest outside spender. name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: It used to be inconceivable to me that America could roll in reverse.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241062%2E444211%2ETCslBI)
Although the conditions for this election continue to be strong – Trump is unpopular, Republican candidates are flailing and Democrats are fighting hard on every front – there were a few setbacks last week that remind us these next 50+ days won’t come easy.
Trump’s efforts to interfere with voting by mail, new Tarrant County polling place closures and Texas’ 1.2-million voter “suspense list” could each determine how free and fair the midterms will be.
But the important thing in working through these challenges is to keep in mind that no loss and no victory in this struggle will be final. We are going to have to keep pushing until we win. And then continue the fight long after we do.
**Back in the old days, say in 2016, it was inconceivable to me that America could roll in reverse.** Maybe progress came too slowly, but the direction was, and always would be, forward.
The big historical waypoints — the 14th amendment, the 19th amendment, the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts, _Roe v. Wade, Obergefell_ — proved that we traveled a one-way road to enlightenment. “The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends towards justice.” All of that.
Of course when Republicans got behind the wheel or tried to drive from the backseat — Reagan, Newt, Bush, Boehner, etc. — they’d slow things down, try to take us off course. Democrats in power at times would fail to deliver on the full promise and potential of government — accepting half measures, mediocrity, ineffectiveness — and that could build up resistance to progress as well. But the inertia of 200+ years of momentum, I thought, was just too much for it to stop completely.
Like millions who supported, campaigned and voted for him, when Obama won the White House in 2008 I thought our work was through. We could sit back and watch him deliver on our sky high expectations. Now we were really going to move forward!
But then eight years later, Trump won the White House on a vision that dispensed with choosing the right or left fork in the road, dispensed with forward motion altogether. The entirety of his vision was limited to what could be found in America’s rearview mirror. In 2016 we lost both the election and the illusion of inevitable progress.
**But the wakeup could have come earlier, if we’d been paying attention.**
Three years before, the Roberts Court had overturned much of the Voting Rights Act. The one that John Lewis nearly lost his life to win, that LBJ staked so much of his presidency to sign, that took our country nearly 90 years to pass. In _Shelby v Holder_ they decided that racism and election interference no longer threatened the ability of every American to fairly and freely vote. In her scathing dissent, Justice Ginsburg wrote that discarding the law which had produced the closest thing to a true democracy in American history “is like throwing away your umbrella in a rainstorm because you are not getting wet.”
_President Barack Obama hugs John Lewis on the 50th Anniversary of Bloody Sunday and the Selma to Montgomery civil rights marches, at the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama. (Photo by Pete Souza)_
Within minutes of the decision, Texas imposed the most restrictive voter ID law in the country, disenfranchising more than 600,000 citizens who, all of a sudden, couldn’t meet the state’s standard for proving who they were. Over the decade that followed Texas also closed more than 700 polling places, twice the number of the next most restrictive state, and almost all of them in African American and Latino neighborhoods. Congressional districts were racially gerrymandered, voting by mail was restricted and voting locations were moved miles away from colleges and universities.
Without the protection of the Voting Rights Act, politicians were free to not only pick their voters, but they could now choose who could vote in the first place.
It was a preview of what was to come from the first Trump term. Like the _Shelby_ decision that imperiled the fundamental right to vote, the attacks on immigrants, on the Constitution and the rule of law reversed progress that had been won at extraordinary sacrifice over decades.
When _Roe_ was overturned in 2022 by the justices appointed during Trump’s first term, another longstanding milestone of progress was toppled — like the loss of voting rights, unthinkable until it happened. Because only in a fever could you dream that a victory won by three courageous Texas women in 1973 – persuading an all-male Supreme Court that American women had a right to make their own decisions about their own bodies – could be reversed by an adjudicated sexual abuser 50 years later.
But maybe there was virtue in these losses. The scales fell and we were able to see our country and our politics for what it was, not what we wished it to be. We understood that as hard-fought as our forward progress had been, it could be rolled back at the turn of a single election.
What’s been happening over these last ten years and what’s coming to a head right now in our country — this battle between authoritarianism and democracy, between cruelty and decency — is what it’s going to be like for a long time. Maybe the way it’s always been, maybe the way it will always be.
Earlier this summer we briefly celebrated when a federal judge ordered the Trump administration to stop interfering with vote by mail, only to see the Supreme Court decide that, because the Postal Service had yet to publish rules around mail-in ballots, the plaintiffs had no standing. Then, once those rules were published, that same judge again enjoined the administration from interfering with voting by mail. [Now Trump is appealing this to a Supreme Court stacked with his chosen justices. They could decide the issue as soon as next week.](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/68174?t=3&akid=241062%2E444211%2ETCslBI)
We breathed a sigh of relief last month when the Republican majority on the Tarrant County Commissioner’s Court reversed course on their plan to close nearly half of the county’s polling locations thanks to the outrage from their constituents. This is the third-largest county in Texas, home to Fort Worth and a true bellwether in our state’s politics. [Recently the Court reconvened and decided to close more than 90 of them anyway.](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/68175?t=4&akid=241062%2E444211%2ETCslBI)
And as Democratic candidates pull ahead in poll after poll in Texas, as we register tens of thousands of new voters and as we overcome attacks on the voting rights of naturalized citizens, [we’ve just learned that more than 1.2 million Texans are now on a “suspense list,”](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/68176?t=5&akid=241062%2E444211%2ETCslBI) meaning that they are required to take action to remedy their registration or may have a hard time voting in November. I met a mother and son in San Antonio who told me that of the four members of their household, the three that reliably vote in the Democratic primary are now in suspense, while the one who votes in the Republican primary is not. I am hearing stories like this across the state.
Each of these setbacks are serious but not defining. And if we fight back, they will not defeat us.
In vote by mail, it’s possible that the Supreme Court rules against Trump and upholds the injunction, allowing ballots to go out under the status quo ante and protecting the millions of Americans who rely on this form of voting. And even if they choose to create extraordinary chaos by siding with Trump and allowing the new USPS rules to go into effect, we can work to educate every voter about their rights under these new rules and encourage those who can to vote in person.
In Tarrant County, we can acknowledge that for many voting will be much harder and then work to help those most impacted. The polling site at UT Arlington, home to more than 42,000 students, was one of those closed this week. In response, our organization Powered by People will be at UTA this week registering students, updating registrations for those on the suspense list and personally staying in touch with every one of them to guide them to the next closest polling site.
And when it comes to the more than one million registered Texans on the suspense list who are now unsure about their registration status, we are relentlessly showing up to meet them where they are – in person and virtually – to help them check their status and update their registration. We’ll add to their numbers through the voter registration program we’re running across the state that’s bringing in a record number of new voters. As of this spring there are 1.5 million more voters on the rolls than there were in Trump’s last midterm.
We’ve just got to keep fighting, through the losses, past the wins. It never ends. Maybe the moral arc bends but only when we pull on it.
If we win the Texas governor’s race and pick up enough seats in the state house, we can end the voter purges and allow people to register to vote online or automatically when they turn 18 or become a citizen.
If we elect Democrats to the Tarrant County Commissioners Court we can restore the polling places for as long as we keep a majority. It’ll take hustling every election cycle to keep good people in, bad people out.
If we defeat Trump and the MAGA movement at the polls — like electing James Talarico to be the 51st vote in the Senate — we can pass a new Voting Rights Act that will protect all eligible voters and means of voting, including by mail. And those political rights will stand for as long as we vigorously defend them, against authoritarians and against our own complacency.
No victory, no matter how justified, how righteous, is ever permanent.
That’s a lot of work, a lot of fighting in front of us.
[**Powered by People is committed to that fight. If you’re with us, please consider donating any amount to support our work today.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260913.GL7WrI&refcode=ema20260913-241062&t=6&akid=241062%2E444211%2ETCslBI)
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260913.GL7WrI&refcode=ema20260913-241062&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=25&akid=241062%2E444211%2ETCslBI)**
Thank you,
Beto

If we elect Democrats to the Tarrant County Commissioners Court we can restore the polling places for as long as we keep a majority. It’ll take hustling every election cycle to keep good people in, bad people out. If we defeat Trump and the MAGA movement at the polls — like electing James Talarico to be the 51st vote in the Senate — we can pass a new Voting Rights Act that will protect all eligible voters and means of voting, including by mail. And those political rights will stand for as long as we vigorously defend them, against authoritarians and against our own complacency. No victory, no matter how justified, how righteous, is ever permanent. That’s a lot of work, a lot of fighting in front of us. Thank you, Beto

body:

Peter,
The Left has a playbook: create panic, expand government power, then tell you it’s for your own good.
[Ohio saw that playbook during COVID. And the person who ran it is now the Democrats’ candidate for governor: Amy “Dr. Lockdown” Acton.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
---
[](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
---
We will NEVER forget how she treated us.
Acton claimed 100,000 Ohioans were already infected, only to walk the number back within 24 hours. But the panic had already set in, and fear became the justification for sweeping government control.
Schools shut down across the state. Businesses had to fight the government in court just to survive. Families were told where they could go and how they could live.
[That wasn’t leadership. That was a bureaucratic takeover.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
And now the same political kabal that pushed lockdowns wants to rewrite history and send Ohio’s Anthony Fauci to the Governor’s mansion.
And here’s the bigger truth: The same people who shut down Ohio also believe the government should control your economy. They use “equity” as a smokescreen to treat your private property like a government ATM. They create a crisis, and then demand you pay for it.
[Vivek is running for Governor of Ohio to build a firewall against that radicalism.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
But we cannot be asleep at the wheel. The Democrat machine is flooding Ohio with money. And the latest poll shows Vivek is trailing by just ONE point.
[Peter, if you believe you — not the government — should be in charge of your life, help Vivek stop these tyrants in their tracks:](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)

Team, When it comes to campaigns, it’s usually the big stuff that makes the news. Thousands of doors knocked. Tens of thousands of mail pieces sent. Big TV ad buys reaching voters across the district. But none of that happens without a whole lot of small stuff behind the scenes. Every day Pat and our team are out on the campaign trail, there are dozens of little expenses that keep everything moving:
* Rent and utilities for our field office
* Gas and vehicle maintenance
* Event space booking fees
* Chairs
* Microphones
* Paper
* Printer toner
* Postage
* Umbrellas

When I was 20, I had a miscarriage. I didn’t understand what was happening to me. I was bleeding so heavily that I had to sit on a newspaper on my way to the hospital. The doctors told me I needed a D&C;, a standard medical procedure used after a miscarriage to prevent infection and dangerous bleeding. **It was medical care. It was necessary. And it saved me.** A few years later, when I was 24, I gave birth to my son. It was a traumatic birth. I went into shock and nearly died. My son nearly died, too. But I survived because a nurse acted immediately. Then at 25, I became pregnant again, despite using birth control. I was terrified of going through another complicated pregnancy and birth. So, I made the decision that was right for my health and pregnancy: I had an abortion. **Women of color like me are more likely to die during pregnancy and childbirth by staggering margins.** For families that live in states with abortion bans, maternal mortality has climbed even higher. I’m grateful I could receive abortion care and that my doctor could provide it. But right now, extremists are stripping many Americans of these basic freedoms, especially in the south. That’s why we need protections for birth control, miscarriage management, prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, fertility care, and abortion care. I hope you’ll join me in supporting Virginians for Reproductive Freedom’s historic fight to enshrine reproductive freedom into Virginia’s Constitution this November. **[Friend, will you support this powerful movement with a contribution of $10, $15, $25, or more today?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139133777/646336709/241827350?refcode=091026&sourceid=1052158&ms=091326&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNMDEvMS8xMTg5NjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTVlMTYxZWMtYWJhZi1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=dOeP4aR26rfBNbomL7vjtDLG3JqJbHgGKYpD4-Ih3ls=)**

body:
Republicans are counting on voter discouragement. Let’s prove them wrong.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**First:** There was a shift in Texas.
Democrats showed up with a mission during the March primary. In this year’s primary, **Democrats cast more ballots than Republicans** for the first time since the 2020 open Democratic presidential primary.
**Then:** They shut down polling locations in Tarrant County on Election Day during the Primary election.
Tarrant County is Texas’ third most populous district. A plan was just approved to shut down 92 polling locations for November’s midterms. This is roughly a 30% reduction in locations for constituents to cast ballots, leaving only 224 locations to serve the county’s 1.3 million voters.
**Now:** They’ve added millions of voters to the “voter suspense list.”
These tactics are designed to discourage people from voting. They’re betting on people staying home, discouraged. **The stakes of this race are only increasing.** It’s clear Texans want real change, and Republicans are doing everything in their power to stop this.
**But we won’t let that happen.** New polling shows a tie between Gina and Greg Abbott, and our movement has more momentum than ever. We’re counting on your support to help continue this momentum through November.

clean_body: Republicans are counting on voter discouragement. Let’s prove them wrong. Peter, First: There was a shift in Texas. Democrats showed up with a mission during the March primary. In this year’s primary, Democrats cast more ballots than Republicans for the first time since the 2020 open Democratic presidential primary. Then: They shut down polling locations in Tarrant County on Election Day during the Primary election. Tarrant County is Texas’ third most populous district. A plan was just approved to shut down 92 polling locations for November’s midterms. This is roughly a 30% reduction in locations for constituents to cast ballots, leaving only 224 locations to serve the county’s 1.3 million voters. Now: They’ve added millions of voters to the “voter suspense list.” These tactics are designed to discourage people from voting. They’re betting on people staying home, discouraged. The stakes of this race are only increasing. It’s clear Texans want real change, and Republicans are doing everything in their power to stop this. But we won’t let that happen. New polling shows a tie between Gina and Greg Abbott, and our movement has more momentum than ever. We’re counting on your support to help continue this momentum through November. name: Roy Cooper
subject: You’re someone I can count on
body:
Republicans aren’t going to give up this seat without a fight.

I can't thank you enough, Peter.
You haven’t chipped in to my U.S. Senate campaign yet, but I appreciate that you’d even take the time to read this.
Because of you, momentum is on our side – so much so that experts say North Carolina is our best chance to flip a GOP-held Senate seat this cycle. **So with just two days to go until our mid-month deadline, I’m turning to the folks I can count on for help one more time:**
[**_If you already understand the stakes of this race, will you please make your first donation of $5 now to my campaign?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1326&amount=5&t=8&akid=3404%2E124072%2EPxVTiO)

My opponent, Michael Whatley, was cherry-picked by President Trump to run against me – and Senate control comes down to who wins this seat.
Since the Senate GOP’s top super PAC went live with a new batch of false attack ads, they’re now spending more here in our state to defeat me than almost anywhere else in the country. **Yet with a recent poll showing the race is statistically tied once again, their scheme is working.**
We can’t afford for billionaires and corporations to buy this seat for an out-of-touch DC insider and lobbyist like Whatley – but without your help to reach our $2.5 million goal, we won’t be able to compete like we should with the onslaught of MAGA dark money.
[**_Please, Peter, can you chip in $5, or any amount right now to help me fight back, surge ahead and win in North Carolina? I can’t flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008 without you._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1326&amount=5&t=10&akid=3404%2E124072%2EPxVTiO)

Friend, I just made a risky decision. I hope you’ll help me prove it was the right one.

**[With less than 72 hours to reach our $200,000 mid-month goal, I’m taking a leap of faith in this grassroots team.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139134816/646340067/-540544497?amounts=10,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk225&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZWMwOTAxYTEtYjJhZi1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hx06cX1OuM5Y70j7J5DDkg4eIK1Gw8ldP7DPh1qAeGU=) Let me explain.**

After our debate yesterday, Roger Marshall’s allies are going to pour _even more_ money into negative attack ads to stop our momentum. While we’re getting our own message out as far and wide as we can, here’s the reality: They're **outspending us**. In a big way.
My team tells me we need to step up our efforts ASAP to correct the record — not just to keep this race a dead heat, but to pull ahead and win.

**That’s why I just gave the go-ahead to _increase_ our ad buy and get-out-the-vote efforts. It’s what we need to do to win. name: The Turning Point USA Team
subject: Faith, truth, and the next generation
body:
What this says about this moment in America | | | |
---
| | | Peter,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

President Trump has been trying everything his advisors can think of -- _including blocking a bipartisan housing relief bill_ \-- to press Congress to advance **stalled legislation that** **purports to address his often-repeated --_and equally debunked_ \-- claims of widespread election fraud.** There are stats from the conservative, right-wing Heritage Foundation below that prove it. The SAVE America Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms. **This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote,** and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks.

Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. **And that’s the point.** The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for**** all voters, including:
---
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

Peter, it’s been a tough year. Ever since Donald Trump set off an unprecedented mid-decade gerrymandering crisis, the National Democratic Redistricting Committee has been in overdrive. We’ve used every tool at our disposal to fight back and level the playing field. **As we approach the next phase of this fight at the ballot box, one question I keep hearing from supporters is,[_“Do my $5 donations really help?”_ My answer couldn’t be clearer: Absolutely.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139136160/646343809/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_AGOathRemarks_email_20260913-NDRC-Tier1-AGOathRemarks_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260913-NDRC-Tier1-AGOathRemarks_&utm_campaign=AGOathRemarks&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc3NWU4NzM3LWI4YWYtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWYxZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=AmwUJcFRTSKdfzoD6TTjAJaTifdx8GDdbdYrVEB8yxM=)** I’ve held a lot of important titles over my life — Attorney General, Chief Judge, Deputy Attorney General, U.S. Attorney — but **I now hold the most important title of all of them:_American citizen._** The power we have as American citizens is too often underestimated and minimized. A $5 donation viewed in isolation may not seem significant. But if everyone reading this email came together with $5 contributions, it would fund our work through the rest of the midterm elections. That’s the power that each of us has. I understand that people can be a little pessimistic about whether or not we’re going to be able to stop Republican gerrymanders and get back to a system that’s fair and truly representative. I say history should be our guide. We just celebrated the 250th anniversary of the time a bunch of people got together and decided to take on the mightiest empire in the world to form this nation. I’m sure they had doubts along the way and asked themselves, “Can we pull this off?” We’re celebrating today because they didn’t let it stop them. When women decided that they wanted the right to vote, surely they had doubts about making it happen. I’m sure there were times when Dr. King, John Lewis, and Diane Nash must have thought, “Can we rip down a system of American apartheid?” And yet, they mobilized millions and changed the course of history forever. I always come back to this quote from Dr. King: “The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends towards justice.” But the reality is, it doesn't bend on its own. It only bends when people like us put our hands on that arc and pull it towards justice. [**And a donation to the cause of defending democracy is one way in which you can put your hand on that arc and pull it.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139136162/646343811/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_AGOathRemarks_email_20260913-NDRC-Tier1-AGOathRemarks_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260913-NDRC-Tier1-AGOathRemarks_&utm_campaign=AGOathRemarks&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc3NWU4NzM3LWI4YWYtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWYxZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=AmwUJcFRTSKdfzoD6TTjAJaTifdx8GDdbdYrVEB8yxM=) **So whether you’re donating $5, making phone calls, writing postcards, or trying to get your friends to the polls — all these small individual actions might seem insignificant on their own. clean_body: I’m asking you to step up with a donation of $5 or more | Peter, it’s been a tough year. Ever since Donald Trump set off an unprecedented mid-decade gerrymandering crisis, the National Democratic Redistricting Committee has been in overdrive. We’ve used every tool at our disposal to fight back and level the playing field. As we approach the next phase of this fight at the ballot box, one question I keep hearing from supporters is,= I’ve held a lot of important titles over my life — Attorney General, Chief Judge, Deputy Attorney General, U.S. Attorney — but I now hold the most important title of all of them:American citizen. The power we have as American citizens is too often underestimated and minimized. A $5 donation viewed in isolation may not seem significant. But if everyone reading this email came together with $5 contributions, it would fund our work through the rest of the midterm elections. That’s the power that each of us has. I understand that people can be a little pessimistic about whether or not we’re going to be able to stop Republican gerrymanders and get back to a system that’s fair and truly representative. I say history should be our guide. We just celebrated the 250th anniversary of the time a bunch of people got together and decided to take on the mightiest empire in the world to form this nation. I’m sure they had doubts along the way and asked themselves, “Can we pull this off?” We’re celebrating today because they didn’t let it stop them. When women decided that they wanted the right to vote, surely they had doubts about making it happen. I’m sure there were times when Dr. King, John Lewis, and Diane Nash must have thought, “Can we rip down a system of American apartheid?” And yet, they mobilized millions and changed the course of history forever. I always come back to this quote from Dr. King: “The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends towards justice.” But the reality is, it doesn't bend on its own. It only bends when people like us put our hands on that arc and pull it towards justice. = So whether you’re donating $5, making phone calls, writing postcards, or trying to get your friends to the polls — all these small individual actions might seem insignificant on their own. Together, they create a nation. They change the world. And that’s why I remain optimistic. = Thank you, Eric H. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids, I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They're everything to me. They're the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I've committed my life and career to. And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father Almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. I refuse to look my kids in the eye someday and tell them I gave up when it mattered most. Because nothing — I repeat — nothing is more important to me than fighting off the vicious leftist attacks against the soul of our country. The left hates you. They hate your vote. They hate MAGA for putting America First. And they will do anything — lie, cheat, steal, destroy — to ensure your children inherit a country you won't even recognize. Peter, today I'll make the same promise to you that I've made to myself, to my wife, and to my children: As long as I live, I will continue to FIGHT to preserve the soul of our country. No force on Earth will push me to abandon my mission and calling. Not the attacks. Not the exhaustion. Not the constant pressure to give up and go home. Believe me, I'm not someone who finds it easy to ask for support. Texting and emailing you like this is the last thing I thought I'd have to do when I ran for Congress. But the country we love is on the brink of destruction, and God has put it on my heart to fight with all that I have — even when that means swallowing my pride and asking for help. This is more than a polite request. This is now a final plea for your support. Sincerely, Congressman Brandon Gill (R) TX-26 | | | Paid for by Brandon Gill for Texas | | PO BOX 827 Arlington, VA 22216 |

Peter, Last week, my wife Karen and I climbed 110 floors to honor the 343 firefighters who lost their lives on 9/11. As I climbed, I kept thinking about those firefighters rushing up crowded stairwells with heavy gear while everyone else was trying to get down. Their courage, sacrifice, and belief in something greater than themselves remain almost impossible to comprehend.

I had the honor of visiting Ground Zero soon after the attacks. I watched rescue workers search the rubble for any sign of life. I saw pleas written in the dust: “Please save my mom. Please save my dad.” I met a weary father keeping vigil for his two firefighter sons. When I asked how long he would stay, he told me, “I’m not leaving until they find my sons.” Tragically, they never did.

Those memories have never left me. Neither has the way Americans came together in our shared grief.

As we continue to honor the memory of the lives lost on 9/11, the families impacted, and our brave first responders and service members, I wanted to share with you two conversations I think you may find interesting:
1\. [On my SiriusXM show I interviewed actor Gary Sinise](http://links.johnkasich.com/s/c/MisyQqDdpK4yF4--7TkWd545McBvtGTn25GWD5SbXOrepXV_A2MdIHdPh4ZeQrmJqPTHBb0tH7UJleescKnjmmTppMWqZa07iZdTFI7zPS_1mQiywJeTT6Kp7DT48EjAUWGoE2Gqtm9Woon1p9mLlMmNQQhBWC1C3ai5GVYOgCj2v7GdUbatMZcwG7udmuT5jafpDZodOyOVcW-Hq2BlENyVwFIE5cfhCbl7_n1nI_2hEJVn_LHIb3DPrqebOtuY4phl4541DzxtDhZpB-JnTU3gfWVgmWXwwaSLQlENRRWrPjvF6Ac6i7XnsGevEw8QZffbdmFPDSvUvVi5UfuoZkIHxHsfNlkCiI-NvoYanOWBp-0etQzRx-FuSoBLA0ELK1K47deYt6jP/DrYL0_xcrxd6Ltj98s_31j9jziCV30eo/24) to learn more about the work he and his foundation have done to support 9/11 families and service members. SiriusXM does require a subscription to listen live or to past episodes, but you can sign up for a free three month trial so you can listen to the episodes. [Get started here](http://links.johnkasich.com/s/c/HhPJhr-wHtKp8jEA8NSwPxbP7O1_3bqiOSC6V-QAnzo9aFt0iPWBJmCUm1jWrplya4rb2N6TDHiLYKrgiks0FlbceC2qvlS2pjuRHjAKdoBRNO-VM-EiIcipG_QG9dpPMw0dqiuR26g9gyxjjZvLnTOlb-SnT2fqXCOcQxAW_1zEn3Al9GSG_0xZwjs4hl_dATwWHuscZVRoSQzAHEglWC8qEiRt6LM99M_CwKanNhstnexF4AfD8QJY59WAq97CDl1_D0_EKfxFu5JtzMSirWjMim452OP3PFCa8__popJ9aVYkBhTLzYj4z9X_1zibqs-vxAsiRhgSNoEP9x1xqJtzolVvwpLMwQ6oUzGun4OONGDYC7ELcNKBHNtJHRk0L3WR1GdIAVAQ/k2RLmAvDMc4pHoW-U_Mw08uvlBBMg5YG/24).

2\. For my free substack newsletter, [I interviewed veteran journalist Carol Lin](http://links.johnkasich.com/s/c/R96ywC03CUtiYGrvA-UgN7qe4yErCpGLy_xQsfClyJM5ErKp94MdOUtuQFgDJ7ZrsexP-vOLFphnWls_4u7JZVrd5t-19Qto54N5-RF8fA5qXz99aM2EC-ABaAtpwdEwRtPupJW_0m9sdShpPxfVLC9eeH2962uukCrKa415B5r_v8wS4ORDys6oe483eM4uCAv-4eL8YBZHjhv_aXVu7g9bI5Dn-h6Z3_w5vsP95eSGYqBIccbtlT_NkHWSr2SUoz-AudGW-P6k-2mE5ys5qpuwYpKmET7RoPJ0JLTVxrPElNJFMqOJ-VSZVYDuj9E_S1Qi9XT-D-WV_4RBrt9nM2t0hA_CYD0rEsEQU70alVqnnBwopVxLUCnUnvO88b7Xxcg6BmNqbB3MMOAc6LiLzi8rTtHB2aLiLGfImpcf1FJ3ibhheC1ZvDACOJuVtR5bj-xFdWar5qcjM96SyLBtyJE/YiV4z0Rhbd0mzu9dSaEUPxZMbtJmS5gp/24) about what it was like reporting in real-time on the 9/11 attacks, and how journalism has changed since 2001. [Listen to our conversation here](http://links.johnkasich.com/s/c/-rCmvZuYpCXuJgcQsdNFD7NUQbaIs7mP9lJCNy3yiLoG1VgFmhfeYuv6rohbSSfMiXtpEfunrCZL0yMb6KeZFCCAqvPi7UKPZZEYYDu-trtMwr6szIt2L6XfXpvQtsZu_eLaYPjJMdVTfrbXek87QbbrJU0yltdx7MLVkwBXD4cSRAEAYMq9SBZ6L2FKgk9RjHwK_G3SrhGyFFYeMdEXQxb_lz3sieH36fGvyPE1J6Z0yPkxfV-LJ-JdHnTAZK-A6E8SlGURelDEoy6xq3nHsnyACc7YYL5vbxTwHgr8QWGp8daWo6unMxb-c07hO5SIJg614AbIHsJL6CEBB3VZG1AIJTkE_8stMPFWVJuz9G83Ye39y19CAx9fKT4WaxcqM0byk7BvYsPsalWbben1lmS1vumBR6RUxE2BXMC6UCTfWdOq6i_AZBuJwTvjPvjETLY0wI7fJrQhvFYwNqy1Wrk/HJtmd9vyGePe7pQcCw_m1leiv6EndaD6/24).
Lin is a veteran anchor and correspondent for CNN and ABC News. Best known for being the first national anchor to report the 9/11 attacks, her career spanned the aftermath of the Kosovo War, the fall of the Taliban, and the war in Iraq. A recipient of the Emmy, Peabody, and Alfred I. duPont Awards, Lin also earned acclaim for her investigative work on human trafficking and the LA Riots.

We'll have more updates for you soon. Thank you for your ongoing support. -John

Their courage, sacrifice, and belief in something greater than themselves remain almost impossible to comprehend. I had the honor of visiting Ground Zero soon after the attacks. I watched rescue workers search the rubble for any sign of life. I saw pleas written in the dust: “Please save my mom. Please save my dad.” I met a weary father keeping vigil for his two firefighter sons. When I asked how long he would stay, he told me, “I’m not leaving until they find my sons.” Tragically, they never did. Those memories have never left me. Neither has the way Americans came together in our shared grief. As we continue to honor the memory of the lives lost on 9/11, the families impacted, and our brave first responders and service members, I wanted to share with you two conversations I think you may find interesting: 1\. to learn more about the work he and his foundation have done to support 9/11 families and service members. SiriusXM does require a subscription to listen live or to past episodes, but you can sign up for a free three month trial so you can listen to the episodes. . 2\. For my free substack newsletter, about what it was like reporting in real-time on the 9/11 attacks, and how journalism has changed since 2001. . Lin is a veteran anchor and correspondent for CNN and ABC News. Best known for being the first national anchor to report the 9/11 attacks, her career spanned the aftermath of the Kosovo War, the fall of the Taliban, and the war in Iraq. A recipient of the Emmy, Peabody, and Alfred I. duPont Awards, Lin also earned acclaim for her investigative work on human trafficking and the LA Riots. We'll have more updates for you soon. Thank you for your ongoing support. -John | Follow Me on Social Media: | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | Paid for by Kasich for America, not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. www.JohnKasich.com

name: Team Molly
subject: Did you see this?
body:
Dear Peter, I wanted to make sure you saw our email from earlier this week: **Lowering costs for Vermonters starts with a plan.** Molly’s priorities are clear: protecting fundamental rights, supporting working families, and lowering costs for Vermonters. Vermont is an incredibly special place to live, but too many Vermonters are being squeezed every day by the rising cost of living. From housing and health care to the everyday costs of raising a family, we need leaders who are focused on making life more affordable for everyone. **_Here’s how Molly will do it_ :**
* **Address** healthcare costs by advancing universal primary care
* **Build** and rehabilitate housing Vermonters can afford
* **Grow** our Vermont workforce
* **Support** energy resilience and independence

Lowering costs, and addressing property taxes, won’t happen with one quick fix. It requires tackling these interconnected challenges. Take health care costs, specifically health insurance premiums. We know hospital costs continue to drive premiums higher. By investing in universal primary care, we can keep Vermonters out of costly emergency rooms for basic and preventive care, lower health care costs, incentivize wellness over profit from illness, and provide relief for working families, employers, and taxpayers. More affordable housing means a stronger workforce, more businesses, and more Vermonters able to call Vermont home. By building and rehabbing homes, we grow our economy, strengthen our communities, and expand our tax base. Molly gets it. As she often says, “We aren’t going to birth our way out of our demographic crisis.” We need to welcome new people to Vermont—and Molly has been doing exactly that. Through her work with the Vermont Afghan Alliance and community partners, she helped welcome more than 650 Afghan allies into Vermont’s workforce and communities. And as we’ve always said, we’re not just building a campaign to win in November. We’re building a broad coalition of Vermonters with unique talents, experiences, and ideas to tackle these challenges. It will take all of us. **[If you agree, please consider chipping in today to help elect Molly and put her plan to lower costs into action for Vermonters.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139136554/646345175/679520187?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlYTlkMmQxMC1iZGFmLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1XhMv8setpPW0B7ugrcOkkgqpwNXK458JaZOM46-UzA=)**

**I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home. I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country. After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents. Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser. I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first. Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors. I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country. Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump? For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening. But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question: Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous? In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public. I was terrified. I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat. name: Roy Cooper
subject: You stood out from the crowd
body:
I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1323&source=&t=1&akid=3423%2E124072%2EXwzqt0) | | | |
---
Peter, I’m not reaching out to everyone today – just a select few, including you.
My team was going through our supporter records, and we noticed how yours stood out from the crowd. You’re one of my most attentive grassroots supporters. You’ve been getting these emails for a while now, and we see you're keeping up with the latest on this election. I want you to know that _I know_ how engaged you’ve been with our campaign and how much I appreciate it.
**Today, I’m asking you to take the next step. Here's why:**
Grassroots fundraising has really slowed down these last few weeks, and it couldn’t come at a worse time. Republican super PACs have already been pouring just over $100 million so far into North Carolina to defeat me, and now, a super PAC aligned with President Trump is unleashing millions more to double down on their attacks.
Since recent polls show this race statistically tied, we need to turn this around fast – and the first step is reaching our $2.5 million mid-month goal on Tuesday night. [**_Will you chip in $5 right now to help us get there in time? The stakes could not be higher._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1323&amount=5&t=8&akid=3423%2E124072%2EXwzqt0)
North Carolina is the best chance Democrats have to flip one of the four seats we need to take back the Senate, so if we lose here, we lose our shot at flipping the majority. The only way we’ll avoid that is by building the resources to compete with the massive amounts of GOP spending.
**Unlike my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley, I’m not a Washington DC insider who can rely on his billionaire connections to buy this Senate seat. I’m depending on people like you, giving what you can, when you can, at crucial moments like this.**
_With a little more than 48 hours to close the gap, Peter, I need you._
[**_Time’s running out, so I’m personally asking: Will you please chip in your first $5 donation to my campaign today so we can reach our ambitious mid-month goal, flip North Carolina’s critical seat and help Democrats secure the Senate majority?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1323&amount=5&t=9&akid=3423%2E124072%2EXwzqt0)

**July 1, 2019**
My husband and I watched Scranton’s former mayor resign in disgrace after pleading guilty to federal corruption charges, criminal conspiracy, bribery, and attempted extortion. **August 21, 2019**
I announced my Independent campaign for Scranton mayor and against the local Democratic Party’s cronyism. Our campaign was dubbed _Paige Against the Machine._ **November 5, 2019**
I won our historic mayoral campaign, becoming the first female mayor of Scranton after winning a tough election against the local Democratic machine — all while eight months pregnant. **January 6, 2020**
Just two weeks after my daughter Sloane was born, I was sworn in as mayor. In the six years since then, we cleaned up City Hall, balanced the books, cut red tape, and brought hundreds of small businesses and over a thousand homes to our neighborhoods. **September 2, 2025**
We launched this campaign for Congress to challenge Rob Bresnahan's corruption and restore accountability in NEPA. It somehow feels like a lifetime ago and just yesterday. **May 19, 2026**
We advanced to the general election, and I became the official Democratic nominee to take on Rob and his corruption in November. I’m ready to reform Congress the way I reformed Scranton — but I need your help to do it. **November 3rd, 2026**

body:
Democrats didn’t jump into these races because they think it's going to be a walk in the park
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to take back control of Congress this November. If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=1&akid=8762%2E22930333%2Ey8SgPE) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=2&akid=8762%2E22930333%2Ey8SgPE), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=3&akid=8762%2E22930333%2Ey8SgPE). | [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20260913_8762_fr&refcode2=8762_22930333_y8SgPE&akid=8762%2E22930333%2Ey8SgPE)
---
Derek,
I'm personally asking you to [**pitch in $7 to the DNC today**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20260913_8762_fr&refcode2=8762_22930333_y8SgPE&akid=8762%2E22930333%2Ey8SgPE) — but first, I want to explain how this is a pivotal moment in Democrats’ fight to win back control of the U.S. Senate.
Some of the most important races in the entire country are happening in Alaska, North Carolina, Ohio, Michigan, Georgia, Iowa, and Maine.
Democrats didn’t jump into these races because they think it's going to be a walk in the park. They saw that working people everywhere are facing skyrocketing grocery prices, unaffordable healthcare, and a rigged economy built for billionaires, **and they decided to do something about it.**
Now, Republicans and their billionaire backers are pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into attack ads to defeat them. I’m no stranger to the special interests that fight to block our agenda. We’ve kept up the righteous fight for universal childcare, a wealth tax, Medicare for All, and affordable housing. And securing more allies in the House and Senate, and then taking back the White House in 2028, is **essential** to passing an agenda that’s dedicated to improving the lives of the people we serve.
That is why one of the most powerful actions you can take right now is to [**invest in the DNC, the only organization committed to electing Democrats at every single level of government.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20260913_8762_fr&refcode2=8762_22930333_y8SgPE&akid=8762%2E22930333%2Ey8SgPE)
99.7% of the DNC’s donations come from grassroots supporters. We know you can't beat a corrupt system with candidates who are beholden to it. You need an opposition movement powered by people. That’s exactly what the DNC is building.
[**The number of donations matters far more than the size of your gift, because each contribution will send a powerful message that Americans are ready for a government that works for working people. So please, Derek, will you please pitch in $7 or anything you can to the DNC today?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20260913_8762_fr&refcode2=8762_22930333_y8SgPE&akid=8762%2E22930333%2Ey8SgPE)
_If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._

While it was to be expected for Democrats and Leftists to be heavily against President Trump's goal for mass deportations, some on the Right have become blackpilled at the pace of deportations. There have been times when the criticisms have been more than warranted, such as when President Trump floated ICE avoiding farms or hotels and when DHS withdrew extra personnel from Minnesota.
But what we have seen from some on the Right has gone beyond legitimate criticisms. I've seen online posts saying that Trump 2.0 is just a Kamala Harris presidency with a better border or questioning whether the border wall is being built. Even more unhinged responses from a few on the "Right" has been to vote for Democrats as revenge for not Trump not keeping his promises.
We have to remember where we started. Tens of thousands of people were illegally crossing everyday. Thousands more were flying in daily and being released through parole.

Since then, the Trump administration ended those open border policies and has secured funding for the border wall and DHS for the rest of his term. His administration has accomplished this while facing violent resistance from the Left, countless lawsuits, crazy rulings from judges, and pushback from special interests within the Republican party.
## _Watch:_
[](https://substack.com/redirect/727b3428-2919-42f5-80ff-8532f91068c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Perhaps one of the greatest successes is DHS, under Trump, has widely expanded the 287(g) program. This program allows state and local law enforcement to be a force multiplier to locate and arrest illegal aliens in their jurisdiction. Not surprisingly, there were barely any 287(g) agreements during Biden. Today, there are over 2,000 agreements across the country.
Florida is the best example of fully utilizing the 287(g) program. In fact, Florida law enforcement accounts for nearly 40% of all 287(g) arrests.
For anyone doubting how much traction the Trump administration has gotten since the start of his term, you need to do something that I rarely advise: Read the mainstream media.
Story after story, headline after headline from Trump's critics are lamenting how he is making significant progress against illegal and legal immigration abuses.
It was not that long ago that the policies being implemented today were unthinkable, even from a Republican administration. ICE has deported illegal aliens to countries in Africa if they were unable to be returned to their country of origin. I can confirm from my recent reporting in Mexico that those deportations to Africa have been a great deterrent for illegal immigrants.
While there were setbacks in the courts at the start, the Trump administration has been on a roll getting rulings in its favor that cement deportations and immigration restrictions.

In my view, as long as the momentum is working towards undoing the damage, it will give us time to work out the finer details.
It makes zero sense to sit out the midterms or vote for Democrats in order to "send a message" to Trump. The Left has lost their minds over this issue and has gone to the extreme. They're not calling for reforming ICE or DHS, they are calling to get rid of immigration enforcement completely and just allow everyone to come on in.
There is still a long way to go and this won't be fixed under Trump's last term, but Republicans can't let perfect be the enemy of good.

Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today: While it was to be expected for Democrats and Leftists to be heavily against President Trump's goal for mass deportations, some on the Right have become blackpilled at the pace of deportations. There have been times when the criticisms have been more than warranted, such as when President Trump floated ICE avoiding farms or hotels and when DHS withdrew extra personnel from Minnesota. But what we have seen from some on the Right has gone beyond legitimate criticisms. I've seen online posts saying that Trump 2.0 is just a Kamala Harris presidency with a better border or questioning whether the border wall is being built. Even more unhinged responses from a few on the "Right" has been to vote for Democrats as revenge for not Trump not keeping his promises. We have to remember where we started. Tens of thousands of people were illegally crossing everyday. Thousands more were flying in daily and being released through parole. His administration has accomplished this while facing violent resistance from the Left, countless lawsuits, crazy rulings from judges, and pushback from special interests within the Republican party. Watch: Perhaps one of the greatest successes is DHS, under Trump, has widely expanded the 287(g) program. This program allows state and local law enforcement to be a force multiplier to locate and arrest illegal aliens in their jurisdiction. Not surprisingly, there were barely any 287(g) agreements during Biden. Today, there are over 2,000 agreements across the country. Florida is the best example of fully utilizing the 287(g) program. In fact, Florida law enforcement accounts for nearly 40% of all 287(g) arrests. For anyone doubting how much traction the Trump administration has gotten since the start of his term, you need to do something that I rarely advise: Read the mainstream media. Story after story, headline after headline from Trump's critics are lamenting how he is making significant progress against illegal and legal immigration abuses. It was not that long ago that the policies being implemented today were unthinkable, even from a Republican administration. ICE has deported illegal aliens to countries in Africa if they were unable to be returned to their country of origin. I can confirm from my recent reporting in Mexico that those deportations to Africa have been a great deterrent for illegal immigrants. While there were setbacks in the courts at the start, the Trump administration has been on a roll getting rulings in its favor that cement deportations and immigration restrictions. They're not calling for reforming ICE or DHS, they are calling to get rid of immigration enforcement completely and just allow everyone to come on in. There is still a long way to go and this won't be fixed under Trump's last term, but Republicans can't let perfect be the enemy of good.
